findings.statement: Hayward et al. (2017) carried out whole-genome sequencing of cutaneous, acral and mucosal melanomas. Cutaneous melanoma carried many coding and non-coding mutations, with new mutation signatures that the authors attributed to ultraviolet radiation. Significantly mutated genes in cutaneous melanoma included BRAF, CDKN2A, NRAS and TP53. In acral melanoma they were BRAF, NRAS and NF1, and in mucosal melanoma SF3B1.
quotes: The heavily mutated landscape of coding and non-coding mutations in cutaneous melanoma resolved novel signatures of mutagenesis attributable to ultraviolet radiation.
Significantly mutated genes included BRAF, CDKN2A, NRAS and TP53 in cutaneous melanoma, BRAF, NRAS and NF1 in acral melanoma and SF3B1 in mucosal melanoma.

findings.statement: Hayward et al. relevance_reason: Tumor (somatic) exome and transcriptome study of what predicts response to ipilimumab in metastatic melanoma. It does not study germline susceptibility, but it gives context on treatment response in melanoma.

findings.statement: Van Allen et al. (2015) performed whole-exome sequencing on pretreatment tumor biopsies and matched germline samples from 110 patients with metastatic melanoma who were treated with ipilimumab (anti-CTLA-4). Nonsynonymous mutational load was significantly associated with clinical benefit (P = 0.0076), and so was predicted neoantigen load (P = 0.027). Clinical variables such as age, sex, histology and LDH levels did not correlate with response.
quotes: we analyzed whole exomes from pretreatment melanoma tumor biopsies and matching germline tissue samples from 110 patients
Overall, nonsynonymous mutational load was significantly associated with clinical benefit from ipilimumab (P = 0.0076; Mann-Whitney test)
Overall, neoantigen load was significantly associated with clinical benefit (P = 0.027; Mann-Whitney)

findings.statement: Van Allen et al. (2015) found no gene enriched for nonsynonymous somatic mutations, including BRAF and NRAS, in either the patients who benefited from ipilimumab or those who did not. Recurrent neoantigens were rare: 28 of 77,803 unique neoantigens were found only in more than one responder. A previously reported tetrapeptide signature was not enriched among responders.
quotes: No genes were enriched for nonsynonymous mutations, including BRAF and NRAS, in the patient subgroups that had clinical benefit or no clinical benefit (figs. S1 and S2).

Of the 77,803 unique neoantigens in our cohort, 28 (~0.04%) were found in more than one patient having a clinical benefit but were absent in all patients having no clinical benefit or long-term survival (Table 1).

findings.statement: In tumor transcriptome data from 42 patients, Van Allen et al. (2015) found that expression of the cytolytic markers granzyme A (GZMA) and perforin (PRF1) was significantly higher in patients who benefited from ipilimumab (P = 0.042). Expression of CTLA4 and PD-L2 was also higher in this group (P = 0.033 and P = 0.041). The authors suggested that expression of immune checkpoint molecules may correlate with response to immunotherapy.
quotes: Both genes were significantly enriched in the cohort treated with ipilimumab that had clinical benefit compared with the cohort that showed no clinical benefit (P = 0.042; Mann-Whitney) (Fig. 3A).

Expression of CTLA-4 itself and of the programmed cell death 1 ligand 2 (PD-L2), which inhibits peripheral T cell proteins, was also significantly elevated in the cohort that showed clinical benefit compared with the one that showed no clinical benefit (P = 0.033 and P = 0.041; Mann-Whitney) (Fig. 3B).

relevance_reason: Abstract-only functional and tumour-sample study of how BRAF(V600E) melanoma becomes resistant to BRAF/MEK inhibitors through SOX10 loss, TGF-beta signalling and EGFR upregulation. findings.statement: Sun et al. (2014) found that 6 of 16 melanoma tumors acquired EGFR expression after resistance to BRAF or MEK inhibitors developed. In 4 of the 6 EGFR-positive drug-resistant patient samples, they found evidence of SOX10 loss and/or activation of TGF-beta signaling.
quotes: Here we show that 6 out of 16 melanoma tumours analysed acquired EGFR expression after the development of resistance to BRAF or MEK inhibitors.
We find evidence for SOX10 loss and/or activation of TGF-β signalling in 4 of the 6 EGFR-positive drug-resistant melanoma patient samples.

findings.statement: In a chromatin-regulator-focused shRNA screen, Sun et al. (2014) found that suppressing SOX10 in melanoma activated TGF-beta signaling. This led to upregulation of EGFR and PDGFRB, which made the cells resistant to BRAF and MEK inhibitors. EGFR expression or TGF-beta treatment produced slow growth with hallmarks of oncogene-induced senescence, but helped the cells proliferate when BRAF or MEK inhibitors were present.
quotes: we find that suppression of sex determining region Y-box 10 (SOX10) in melanoma causes activation of TGF-β signalling, thus leading to upregulation of EGFR and platelet-derived growth factor receptor-β (PDGFRB), which confer resistance to BRAF and MEK inhibitors.
Expression of EGFR in melanoma or treatment with TGF-β results in a slow-growth phenotype with cells displaying hallmarks of oncogene-induced senescence.
However, EGFR expression or exposure to TGF-β becomes beneficial for proliferation in the presence of BRAF or MEK inhibitors.

findings.statement: In mixed populations of melanoma cells, Sun et al. (2014) found that cells with low SOX10 and high EGFR expression were rapidly enriched in the presence of drug, but this enrichment reversed when the drug was stopped. They suggested that this explains why some BRAF- or MEK-inhibitor-resistant patients may regain sensitivity after a 'drug holiday', and that patients with EGFR-positive melanoma may benefit from re-treatment after one.
quotes: cells with low SOX10 and consequently high EGFR expression are rapidly enriched in the presence of drug, but this is reversed when the drug treatment is discontinued.
identify patients with EGFR-positive melanoma as a group that may benefit from re-treatment after a drug holiday.

relevance_reason: The paper reports recurrent somatic TERT core promoter mutations (C228T, C250T) in 71% of melanomas, with functional reporter assays. This is useful for the somatic molecular genetics of cutaneous malignant melanoma, but it does not cover germline susceptibility.

findings.statement: Huang et al. (2013) analyzed published whole-genome sequencing data from malignant melanomas and found two somatic TERT promoter mutations in 17 of 19 (89%) tumors. Both were C-to-T transitions at dipyrimidine motifs suggesting UV-induced damage: chr5 1,295,228 C>T (C228T) and 1,295,250 C>T (C250T). Both lay within 100 bp of the TERT transcription start site. Sanger sequencing of tumor/normal pairs confirmed the mutations, and an extension set of 51 more melanoma tumor/normal pairs found one of the two mutations in 33 tumors (65%). Altogether, 50 of 70 (71%) melanomas carried a TERT promoter mutation.
quotes: Analysis of whole-genome sequencing data from malignant melanomas revealed two somatic telomerase reverse transcriptase (TERT) gene promoter mutations in 17 of 19 (89%) cases examined.
Within this extension set, 33 tumors (65%) harbored one of the mutations.
Together, these TERT promoter mutations were observed in 50 of 70 (71%; 95% confidence interval: 59 to 82%, Clopper-Pearson method) melanomas examined

findings.statement: Huang et al. (2013) found that C228T and C250T never occurred together in the same melanoma (P = 5.4 x 10(-7)), which suggested the two mutations might be functionally redundant. Two tumors with C228T also had an adjacent C>T change at chr5 1,295,229, indicating a dinucleotide CC>TT transition.
quotes: Moreover, the mutations were mutually exclusive in both the discovery and extension sets (P = 5.4 × 10−7, Fisher’s one-sided exact test).
Two tumors with a C228T transition also contained an adjacent C>T transition (at position chr5, 1,295,229), which is indicative of a dinucleotide CC>TT transition.
This suggests the possibility that the mutations might be functionally redundant.

findings.statement: Huang et al. (2013) showed that C228T and C250T each create the same 11-bp sequence, which contains a consensus binding motif for ETS transcription factors. In luciferase reporter assays in 5 cell lines, each mutation increased transcriptional activity from the TERT core promoter about 2- to 4-fold compared with the wildtype promoter.
quotes: Both C228T and C250T generated an identical 11-bp nucleotide stretch (5′-CCCCTTCCGGG-3′) containing a consensus binding site for E-twenty-six (ETS) transcription factors (GGAA, reverse complement) within the TERT promoter region.
In comparison to the wild-type TERT promoter, both mutations conferred approximately two- to fourfold increased transcriptional activity in five distinct cell line contexts

findings.statement: Huang et al. (2013) proposed that the TERT promoter mutations may be driver events that act through TERT dysregulation in melanoma. Taken together, the mutations were more frequent than BRAF and NRAS mutations. Other recurrent mutations were absent from the 3 kb upstream of the TERT start site, and the mutations were absent from 24 lung adenocarcinomas with similarly high mutation rates. The authors suggested the mutations may be early events in melanoma genesis.
quotes: First, the TERT promoter mutations showed a combined frequency that exceeded those of BRAF and NRAS mutations, which activate known melanoma driver oncogenes.
The high prevalence of C228T and C250T suggests that these TERT promoter mutations may comprise early genetic events in the genesis of melanoma and other cancer types.

findings.statement: Huang et al. (2013) found C228T or C250T in 24 of 150 (16%) cancer cell lines from the Cancer Cell Line Encyclopedia. These included 5 of 6 melanoma lines, 3 of 3 bladder cancer lines, and 4 of 6 hepatocellular cancer lines.
quotes: Overall, 24 CCLE lines (16%) contained either C228T or C250T (mean allelic fraction, 0.61; range, 0.17 to 1.00) (table S1).

An increased frequency in melanoma was again noted (five of six lines tested), with additional evidence suggesting possible heightened prevalence (>25%; one-sided 95% confidence interval) in bladder (three of three lines) and hepatocellular cancer cell lines (four of six lines)

relevance_reason: Identifies a disease-segregating germline TERT promoter mutation in a melanoma-prone family, along with somatic TERT promoter mutations in sporadic melanoma.

findings.statement: Horn et al. (2013) studied a melanoma-prone family using linkage analysis and high-throughput sequencing. They found a germline mutation in the promoter of the TERT gene that segregated with disease. The mutation created a new binding motif for Ets transcription factors and ternary complex factors (TCFs) near the transcription start site. In reporter gene assays, it increased transcription up to twofold.
quotes: We investigated a melanoma-prone family through linkage analysis and high-throughput sequencing and identified a disease-segregating germline mutation in the promoter of the telomerase reverse transcriptase (TERT) gene

The mutation creates a new binding motif for Ets transcription factors and ternary complex factors (TCFs) near the transcription start and, in reporter gene assays, caused up to twofold increase in transcription.

variants.as_reported: germline mutation in the promoter of the TERT gene

findings.statement: In sporadic melanoma, Horn et al. (2013) found recurrent somatic TERT promoter mutations with an ultraviolet signature. They were present in 125 of 168 (74%) cell lines derived from metastatic melanomas, 45 of 53 (85%) corresponding metastatic tumor tissues, and 25 of 77 (33%) primary melanomas. Most of these mutations occurred at 2 positions in the promoter, and they also created binding motifs for Ets/TCF transcription factors.
quotes: observed recurrent ultraviolet signature somatic mutations in 125 of 168 (74%) of human cell lines derived from metastatic melanomas, 45 of 53 corresponding metastatic tumor tissues (85%), and 25 of 77 (33%) primary melanomas
The majority of those mutations occurred at two positions in the TERT promoter and also generated binding motifs for Ets/TCF transcription factors.

variants.as_reported: recurrent ultraviolet signature somatic mutations in the TERT promoter

relevance_reason: This paper models resistance to vemurafenib in BRAF(V600E)-mutant melanoma using patient-derived xenografts. It addresses somatic tumour biology and drug-dosing strategy, not inherited susceptibility. A curator might still cite it in a treatment or molecular section of a melanoma entry.

findings.statement: Das Thakur et al. (2013) selected vemurafenib-resistant tumours by giving vemurafenib continuously to mice carrying a patient-derived xenograft of BRAF T1799A (V600E)-mutant melanoma (HMEX1906). Exome sequencing found no secondary mutations in BRAF, NRAS, KRAS, HRAS or MEK1. Instead, all 9 resistant tumours had higher levels of BRAF(V600E) mRNA and protein, and 1 tumour had BRAF amplification (about 14 copies, compared with about 6 in the parental tumour). Resistant tumours kept a dependency on BRAF(V600E)-MEK-ERK signalling.
quotes: exome sequence analysis failed to reveal secondary mutations in the coding sequences of BRAF, NRAS, KRAS, HRAS or MEK1 in resistant tumours (data not shown).
compared to sensitive tumours, all nine resistant tumours expressed elevated levels of BRAF messenger RNA and protein, with the 45V-RT5 tumour showing the highest levels
the 45V-RT5 tumour was found to have ~14 copies of BRAFT1799A (Fig. 2c), consistent with BRAF amplification as a mechanism of vemurafenib resistance

findings.statement: Das Thakur et al. (2013) found that cells from vemurafenib-resistant tumours became dependent on the drug: they proliferated best at 50 nM vemurafenib. Knocking down BRAF(V600E) partially, to the level seen in parental cells, made the resistant cells sensitive again to vemurafenib and to the MEK inhibitor AZD6244. Raising BRAF(V600E) signalling in parental cells increased pERK but reduced proliferation. The authors concluded that resistance was due to elevated BRAF(V600E) expression, and that this becomes a fitness deficit when the drug is removed.
quotes: a cell-proliferation assay conducted with a range of drug concentrations indicated a bell-shaped response to vemurafenib, with peak proliferation in the resistant cells occurring at 50 nM vemurafenib
These data confirm that resistant tumour cells remain oncogene dependent and that drug resistance is due to elevated expression of BRAF(V600E).
elevated BRAF(V600E) activity in the parental cells led to increased pERK levels but decreased proliferation

findings.statement: In mice, Das Thakur et al. (2013) found that stopping vemurafenib made established drug-resistant melanomas regress. Mice given vemurafenib continuously developed lethal drug-resistant disease within 100 days. None of the mice given the drug intermittently (4 weeks on, 2 weeks off) developed drug-resistant disease over 200 days, and a second patient-derived xenograft (HMEX2613) gave similar results. The authors suggested that intermittent dosing could delay the onset of drug resistance in BRAF-mutant melanoma.
quotes: cessation of drug treatment of mice carrying vemufarenib-resistant melanomas led to clear signs of regression within 10 days after drug withdrawal

mice continuously dosed with vemurafenib developed lethal drug-resistant disease within 100 days after initiation of drug administration. By contrast, none of the mice on the intermittent dosing schedule developed drug-resistant disease over the course of 200 days
these results indicate that intermittent dosing significantly delays the onset of drug resistance by exploiting the fitness deficit shown by drug-resistant tumour cells in the absence of drug

relevance_reason: Functional and clinical-correlation study showing that HGF-MET signalling confers resistance to the BRAF inhibitor vemurafenib (PLX4032) in BRAF-mutant melanoma. This is relevant to drug-resistance mechanisms in melanoma, not to germline susceptibility.

findings.statement: Wilson et al. (2012) tested 41 kinase-addicted human cancer cell lines against 6 receptor tyrosine kinase (RTK) ligands. Nearly all lines could be rescued from kinase-inhibitor-induced growth inhibition by one or more RTK ligands. In BRAF-mutant melanoma cells, HGF was one of very few factors among 446 secreted factors tested that rescued the cells from the BRAF inhibitor PLX4032 (vemurafenib).
quotes: Nearly all of the cell lines tested, representing multiple tissue types and distinct kinase dependencies, could be rescued from drug-induced growth inhibition by one or more RTK ligands (Fig. 1a).
Notably, among 446 tested secreted factors, HGF was among a very small number that could rescue BRAF-mutant melanoma cells from PLX4032 sensitivity (Supplementary Fig. 8).

findings.statement: Wilson et al. (2012) found that HGF significantly reduced PLX4032 sensitivity in 5 of 12 additional BRAF-mutant melanoma cell lines. MET expression correlated with HGF rescue. In rescued lines, HGF reactivated MAPK signalling, and the MET inhibitor crizotinib blocked the rescue. One line (624MEL) had autocrine MET activation, and MET inhibition delayed PLX4032 resistance in this line. Crizotinib also prevented PLX4032 resistance in the A375 and 928MEL lines.
quotes: Among 12 additional BRAF-mutant melanoma cell lines tested, HGF significantly attenuated PLX4032 sensitivity in 5 lines (Fig. 4a).

MET expression was correlated with HGF rescue (Fig. 4a), and HGF re-activated MAPK in lines rescued by HGF, but not in MET-negative HGF-non-rescued cells (Fig. 4b). As anticipated, rescue by HGF was blocked when MET was inhibited by crizotinib
Crizotinib co-treatment also prevented resistance to PLX4032 in two cell lines (A375 and 928MEL) with undetectable phospho-MET, further supporting a role for HGF-activated MET in PLX4032 resistance

findings.statement: In mouse xenografts of the BRAF-mutant melanoma lines 928MEL and 624MEL, Wilson et al. (2012) found that activating MET with the agonistic antibody 3D6 strongly reduced the growth-suppressive effect of PLX4032. Inhibiting MET enhanced PLX4032-induced tumour regression.
quotes: Activation of MET in tumours using the MET-agonistic antibody 3D6 strongly abrogated the growth-suppressive effects of PLX4032 (Fig. 4c).
Inhibiting MET enhanced the effect of PLX4032 on tumour regression (Fig. 4c), with more partial responses observed in the 928MEL model (Supplementary Fig. 10).

findings.statement: Wilson et al. (2012) measured pretreatment plasma HGF in 126 of 132 patients with BRAF-mutant metastatic melanoma treated with PLX4032 in the BRIM2 trial. Higher plasma HGF was associated with worse progression-free survival (hazard ratio 1.42, P less than 0.005) and overall survival (hazard ratio 1.8, P less than 0.001). Because the study was single-arm, the authors could not determine whether higher HGF confers drug resistance, but suggested a potential role for HGF in the response to BRAF inhibition.
quotes: Pre-treatment plasma HGF levels were measured from 126 of the 132 patients enrolled onto the BRIM2 clinical trial (BRAF-mutant metastatic melanoma patients treated with PLX4032).
Increased plasma HGF was associated with worse outcome as measured by progression-free survival (PFS; hazard ratio, 1.42; P <0.005) and overall survival (OS; hazard ratio, 1.8; P <0.001; Fig. 4d, e).
As BRIM2 was a single-arm study in which all patients received PLX4032, it is not possible to determine whether higher HGF levels confer drug resistance

relevance_reason: Mechanistic and clinical-correlation study of innate resistance to RAF inhibitors in BRAF V600E-mutant melanoma through stromal HGF/MET signalling. It is relevant to treatment of melanoma, but it does not address germline susceptibility.

findings.statement: Straussman et al. (2012) developed a co-culture system to test 23 stromal cell types for their effect on how 45 cancer cell lines responded to 35 anticancer drugs. They found that stroma-mediated resistance was common, especially to targeted agents. In BRAF V600E melanoma cell lines, 6 of 18 stromal (fibroblast) lines conferred resistance to the RAF inhibitor PLX4720 through secreted factors. Antibody-array analysis identified hepatocyte growth factor (HGF) as the secreted factor that best correlated with resistance.
quotes: We tested 18 stromal cell lines for their ability to confer resistance of 7 BRAF V600E melanoma cell lines to PLX4720. Of these, 6 fibroblast lines conferred resistance

The factor best correlated with PLX4720 resistance was hepatocyte growth factor (HGF), a well-characterized growth factor whose secretion by mesenchymal cells induces activation of the MET receptor tyrosine kinase

findings.statement: Straussman et al. (2012) performed immunohistochemistry on pretreatment biopsies from 34 patients with BRAF V600E melanoma. HGF was detected in tumor-associated stromal cells in 23 of the 34 patients (68%). Patients with stromal HGF responded significantly worse to BRAF inhibitor treatment than patients without it (P less than 0.05). The single patient with a durable complete response lacked HGF expression.
quotes: HGF was detected in the tumor-associated stromal cells in 23/34 patients (68%)
Indeed, patients with stromal HGF had a significantly poorer response to treatment compared to those lacking expression (P < 0.05; Fig 3c).
only one of the 34 patients had a durable complete response (14 months and continuing), and this patient lacked HGF expression

findings.statement: Straussman et al. (2012) showed that recombinant HGF was both necessary and sufficient to make BRAF-mutant melanoma cells resistant to RAF inhibition. HGF was the only one of 22 receptor tyrosine kinase ligands tested that gave substantial resistance. HGF activated MET and caused sustained reactivation of both the MAPK (ERK) and PI3K/AKT pathways. The authors proposed that, during BRAF inhibition, this happened through RAF1 bypassing BRAF. Blocking HGF with a neutralizing antibody or blocking MET with crizotinib reversed the resistance, and the authors suggested combined RAF plus HGF or MET inhibition as a therapeutic strategy.
quotes: These experiments indicated that HGF is both necessary and sufficient for conferring the resistance phenotype
HGF was the only ligand that conferred substantial resistance to RAF or MEK inhibition

Dual inhibition of RAF and either HGF or MET resulted in reversal of drug resistance, suggesting RAF plus HGF or MET inhibitory combination therapy as a potential therapeutic strategy for BRAF-mutant melanoma.

findings.statement: Nikolaev et al. (2011) used exome sequencing to look for somatic mutations in protein-coding regions in 7 melanoma cell lines, comparing each with germline cells from the same donor. All melanoma samples had high numbers of somatic mutations showing the hallmark of UV-induced DNA repair. This hallmark was absent in the tumor sample-specific mutations of 2 metastases from the same individual.
quotes: We performed exome sequencing to detect somatic mutations in protein-coding regions in seven melanoma cell lines and donor-matched germline cells.
All melanoma samples had high numbers of somatic mutations, which showed the hallmark of UV-induced DNA repair.
Such a hallmark was absent in tumor sample-specific mutations in two metastases derived from the same individual.

findings.statement: Nikolaev et al. (2011) found gain-of-function somatic mutations in MAP2K1 (MEK1) and MAP2K2 (MEK2) in 2 melanomas that carried non-canonical BRAF mutations. The mutations caused constitutive ERK phosphorylation and higher resistance to MEK inhibitors. Screening a larger melanoma cohort showed recurrent somatic MAP2K1 and MAP2K2 mutations at an overall frequency of 8%.
quotes: Two melanomas with non-canonical BRAF mutations harbored gain-of-function MAP2K1 and MAP2K2 (MEK1 and MEK2, respectively) mutations, resulting in constitutive ERK phosphorylation and higher resistance to MEK inhibitors.
Screening a larger cohort of individuals with melanoma revealed the presence of recurring somatic MAP2K1 and MAP2K2 mutations, which occurred at an overall frequency of 8%.

findings.statement: Nikolaev et al. (2011) frequently found somatic missense and nonsense mutations in 3 candidate melanoma genes: FAT4, LRP1B, and DSC1.
quotes: Furthermore, missense and nonsense somatic mutations were frequently found in three candidate melanoma genes, FAT4, LRP1B and DSC1.

relevance_reason: Exome sequencing of metastatic melanoma that identifies somatic MAP3K5 and MAP3K9 mutations, with functional studies. It is somatic tumor genetics, not germline susceptibility, but a curator could cite it in the melanoma entry's molecular genetics section.

findings.statement: Stark et al. (2011) performed whole-exome sequencing of 8 metastatic melanoma cell lines and matched normal lymphoblastoid cell lines and identified 3,215 somatic alterations, of which 2,139 were predicted to alter protein structure. The mutation spectrum, with a predominance of C>T/G>A transitions and CC>TT/GG>AA tandem mutations, matched the signature of ultraviolet light exposure.
quotes: Overall, 3,215 somatic alterations were identified; range 243-523 per sample (Supplementary Table 2).
We observed 17 tandem mutations, including 10 CC>TT/GG>AA alterations, which taken together, is consistent with the mutation signature associated with ultraviolet light exposure.

findings.statement: Stark et al. (2011) screened 85 melanoma cell lines and found somatic nonsynonymous mutations in MAP3K5 in 8 lines (9%) and in MAP3K9 in 13 lines (15%). Taken together, 24% of samples had a mutation in one of the two genes, and with one exception the mutations were mutually exclusive. The mutations were confirmed in matched tumor DNA in all but one sample, and they did not correlate with mutations or deletions of BRAF, NRAS, CDKN2A, PTEN, or TP53.
quotes: A prevalence screen revealed 8/85 melanoma cell lines with somatic non-synonymous mutations in MAP3K5 (8 mutations) and 13/85 cell lines with mutations in MAP3K9 (total of 18 mutations) (Fig. 1).
With the exception of one cell line, mutations in MAP3K5 or MAP3K9 were mutually exclusive (Supplementary Table 6), suggesting they may target the same pathway.
Mutations in MAP3K5 and MAP3K9 were not correlated with mutations/deletions of BRAF, NRAS, CDKN2A, PTEN, or TP53 (Supplementary Table 6).

findings.statement: Stark et al. (2011) found loss of heterozygosity (LOH) at MAP3K5 in 85% (98/115) of melanoma samples and at MAP3K9 in 67% (77/115). They suggested that the high LOH rate, the spread of mutations along each gene, and a MAP3K9 nonsense mutation indicated that the mutations were inactivating. They proposed that the heterozygous mutations reduce gene function through haploinsufficiency.
quotes: showed that 98/115 (85%) and 77/115 (67%) samples had LOH for MAP3K5 or MAP3K9 respectively (Supplementary Fig 3).
The high rate of LOH, the distribution of mutations along the entire length of each gene and the identification of a nonsense mutation in MAP3K9, suggests the mutations are inactivating.

findings.statement: In in vitro kinase assays, Stark et al. (2011) found that the somatic MAP3K9 nonsense mutation W333X reduced kinase activity against myelin basic protein by 95% relative to wildtype. Expression of the mutant in HEK293T cells reduced signaling through MAP2K4/7-JNK and MEK1/2-ERK.
quotes: MAP3K9 K171A and W333X mutants showed a 92% and 95% reduction in kinase activity against MBP relative to the wild type enzyme (p<0.001).
Expression of either mutant MAP3K9 protein (W333X and control K171A) resulted in decreased signaling through MAP2K4/7-JNK and MEK1/2-ERK (Fig. 4b)

findings.statement: Stark et al. (2011) found that the somatic MAP3K5 kinase-domain mutation I780F almost abolished kinase activity (93% reduction). Structural modeling predicted that it affects helix packing in the kinase domain. In HEK293T cells, I780F reduced MAP3K5 phosphorylation and JNK signaling and decreased phospho-MEK1/2.
quotes: MAP3K5 I780F almost completely abolishes kinase activity (93% reduction relative to wild type, p<0.01)
This modelling suggested that the MAP3K5 I780F mutation is likely to affect the packing of helices in the kinase domain (Fig. 2a).

findings.statement: Stark et al. (2011) found that the somatic MAP3K5 mutation E663K, which lies next to the kinase domain and introduces a charge change, modestly but significantly reduced phosphorylation of myelin basic protein (30% reduction). In HEK293T cells it also decreased downstream phospho-MEK1/2.
quotes: while the mutant E663K had lesser yet statistically significant effects on MBP phosphorylation (30% reduction relative to wild type, p<0.05).

findings.statement: Using structural modeling, Stark et al. (2011) predicted effects of three somatic MAP3K9 missense mutations found in melanoma. R160C would disrupt hydrogen bonds with E167, P263L would increase loop flexibility, and E319K would disrupt hydrogen bonding with R393.
quotes: The R160 residue in MAP3K9 forms hydrogen bonds with E167 that would be disrupted by the mutation to cysteine (R160C), while the MAP3K9 P263L mutation is predicted to increase conformational flexibility in the corresponding loop (Fig. 2b).

findings.statement: Stark et al. (2011) found that siRNA knockdown of MAP3K9 in the melanoma cell lines UACC903 and UACC647 increased cell viability after temozolomide treatment. They suggested that reduced MAP3K9 activity can contribute to chemoresistance in melanoma.
quotes: However, upon combination of both siRNA knockdown and TMZ, both cell lines exhibit a resistance phenotype as evidenced by increased cell viability in the presence of both agents compared with drug alone (Fig. 5 bi,ii).
This suggests that attenuated MAP3K9 activity can contribute to chemotherapeutic resistance in melanoma.

findings.statement: Chapman et al. (2011) conducted a phase 3 randomized trial comparing the BRAF inhibitor vemurafenib (960 mg orally twice daily) with dacarbazine in 675 patients with previously untreated, metastatic melanoma with the BRAF V600E mutation. At 6 months, overall survival was 84% in the vemurafenib group and 64% in the dacarbazine group. Vemurafenib was associated with a relative reduction of 63% in the risk of death and of 74% in the risk of death or disease progression (P<0.001 for both), and response rates were 48% versus 5%. After the interim analysis, crossover from dacarbazine to vemurafenib was recommended.
quotes: We conducted a phase 3 randomized clinical trial comparing vemurafenib with dacarbazine in 675 patients with previously untreated, metastatic melanoma with the BRAF V600E mutation.
At 6 months, overall survival was 84% (95% confidence interval [CI], 78 to 89) in the vemurafenib group and 64% (95% CI, 56 to 73) in the dacarbazine group.

vemurafenib was associated with a relative reduction of 63% in the risk of death and of 74% in the risk of either death or disease progression, as compared with dacarbazine (P<0.001 for both comparisons).

findings.statement: In the trial by Chapman et al. (2011), median progression-free survival was 5.3 months with vemurafenib and 1.6 months with dacarbazine (hazard ratio 0.26). A confirmed response occurred in 106 of 219 evaluable patients (48%) in the vemurafenib group, compared with 12 of 220 (5%) in the dacarbazine group. Among 10 vemurafenib-treated patients later found to have BRAF V600K mutations, 4 had a partial response, which the authors said indicated that melanomas with this variant are also sensitive to vemurafenib.
quotes: The estimated median progression-free survival was 5.3 months in the vemurafenib group and 1.6 months in the dacarbazine group.
Ten patients in the vemurafenib group were later found to have BRAF V600K mutations; of these patients, 4 had a partial response (40%).
4 of 10 patients with the BRAF V600K mutation had a response to vemurafenib, indicating that melanomas with this variant are also sensitive to vemurafenib.

findings.statement: Chapman et al. (2011) reported that the common adverse events with vemurafenib were arthralgia, rash, fatigue, alopecia, keratoacanthoma or squamous-cell carcinoma, photosensitivity, nausea, and diarrhea. Cutaneous squamous-cell carcinoma, keratoacanthoma, or both developed in 61 patients (18%) and were treated by simple excision. Overall, 38% of patients needed a dose modification because of toxic effects. The authors speculated that the cutaneous neoplasia may result from vemurafenib's paradoxical activation of the MAPK pathway in cells with wild-type BRAF.
quotes: In the vemurafenib group, a cutaneous squamous-cell carcinoma, keratoacanthoma, or both developed in 61 patients (18%). All lesions were treated by simple excision.

Common adverse events associated with vemurafenib were arthralgia, rash, fatigue, alopecia, keratoacanthoma or squamous-cell carcinoma, photosensitivity, nausea, and diarrhea; 38% of patients required dose modification because of toxic effects.
it is speculated to involve the activating effect of vemurafenib on preneoplastic cells in which wild-type BRAF is further primed by upstream pathway activation.

phenotypes.hpo_label: Squamous cell carcinoma of the skin

findings.statement: Chapman et al. (2011) stated that about 40 to 60% of cutaneous melanomas carry BRAF mutations that constitutively activate MAPK signaling. About 90% of these are V600E, and other activating mutations include V600K and V600R. In their trial, the 675 randomized patients included 20 with non-V600E mutations (19 with V600K and 1 with V600D), which were identified by Sanger and 454 sequencing.
quotes: Approximately 40 to 60% of cutaneous melanomas carry mutations in BRAF that lead to constitutive activation of downstream signaling through the MAPK pathway.
These patients included 20 with non-V600E mutations (19 with V600K and 1 with V600D), as identified on Sanger and 454 sequencing.

relevance_reason: Reports somatic mutations found by exome sequencing of metastatic melanoma tumours: a recurrent TRRAP hotspot mutation and frequent GRIN2A mutations. This adds somatic molecular genetics to the melanoma entry but does not address germline susceptibility.

findings.statement: Wei et al. (2011) performed whole-exome sequencing of 14 matched normal and metastatic tumor DNAs from untreated patients with melanoma. They identified 68 genes that appeared to be somatically mutated at elevated frequency. The mutation spectrum showed a high prevalence of C>T/G>A transitions and CC>TT/GG>AA dinucleotide substitutions, consistent with an ultraviolet light exposure signature. The BRAF V600E mutation was found in 7 of the 14 samples.
quotes: we performed whole-exome sequencing of 14 matched normal and metastatic tumor DNAs. Using stringent criteria, we identified 68 genes that appeared to be somatically mutated at elevated frequency
we observed a total of 116 dinucleotide substitutions; of these, 59 were CC>TT/GG>AA changes, all consistent with the previously documented ultraviolet light exposure signature
the BRAF p.Val600Glu alteration was captured in 7 out of the 14 samples

findings.statement: Wei et al. (2011) identified a recurrent somatic mutation in TRRAP, c.2165C>T (p.Ser722Phe), in 6 of 167 melanomas (about 4%), including the melanoma cell line A375. Sequencing all coding exons of TRRAP in 25 additional melanomas found no further nonsynonymous alterations. The affected residue is highly conserved. Because there were no truncating mutations and all alterations occurred at one position, the authors suggested that TRRAP may be a new oncogene.
quotes: TRRAP harbored a recurrent mutation that clustered in one position (p. Ser722Phe) in 6 out of 167 affected individuals (∼4%)

The recurring mutation in TRRAP was a cytosine to thymine change at position 2,165 of the transcript (uc003upp.1), leading to a serine to phenylalanine substitution at amino acid residue 722 of the protein (p.Ser722Phe).
The positions of the mutations in TRRAP imply that they are likely to be oncogenic, as we observed no truncating mutations, and 100% of the alterations occurred in one location.

findings.statement: Wei et al. (2011) tested the TRRAP Ser722Phe mutation functionally. Mutant TRRAP transformed NIH 3T3 cells more efficiently than wildtype TRRAP. Knocking down TRRAP with shRNA had little effect on melanoma cells with wildtype TRRAP but substantially increased apoptosis, with increased PARP cleavage, in melanoma lines carrying mutant TRRAP (63T and A375). The authors concluded that mutant TRRAP is essential for melanoma cell survival.
quotes: Two weeks after transfection, mutant TRRAP transformed NIH 3T3 cells more efficiently than wild-type TRRAP (Fig. 2a).

Knockdown of TRRAP had minimal effect on the survival of cells expressing wild-type TRRAP but substantially increased apoptosis rates of melanoma lines carrying mutant TRRAP, particularly when the clones were grown in low serum
Thus, mutant TRRAP is essential for melanoma cell survival

findings.statement: Wei et al. (2011) found somatic GRIN2A mutations in 6 of 14 melanomas in the exome discovery screen. In further screening they found 11 more in a prevalence screen of 38 melanomas, 11 of 39 melanomas in validation set 1, and 5 of 32 in validation set 2, plus one mutation in the 501Mel cell line. In total they identified 34 distinct GRIN2A mutations in 135 samples (25.2%). These included 2 mutation clusters (around residues 371-373 and 1073-1076), 3 recurrent alterations (S278F, E371K and E1175K), and 5 nonsense mutations. The authors said the tumorigenic mechanism was unclear, but that the mutation frequency strongly suggested a major role in melanoma.
quotes: In total, we identified 34 distinct GRIN2A mutations in 135 samples (25.2%) (Supplementary Table 4).
In addition, we observed three recurrent alterations (p.Ser278Phe, p.GluE371Lys and p.Glu1175Lys).
the mechanism by which mutations in GRIN2A have a tumorigenic effect is unclear; however, their frequency strongly suggests that they play a major role in melanoma

findings.statement: In a pathway analysis, Wei et al. (2011) found that the glutamate signaling pathway was highly significantly mutated in melanoma. GRIN2A, which encodes an NMDA receptor subunit, and PLCB4 were frequently mutated. The authors suggested that most melanomas had alterations in genes encoding members of the glutamate signaling pathway.
quotes: From this analysis, we found the glutamate signaling pathway to be highly significant.
show that a majority of melanoma tumors had alterations in genes encoding members of the glutamate signaling pathway

relevance_reason: Reports the discovery and Phase 1 clinical efficacy of the BRAF V600E inhibitor PLX4032 (vemurafenib) in BRAF-mutant metastatic melanoma. This is treatment information for the melanoma entry; the paper reports no germline susceptibility data.

findings.statement: Bollag et al. (2010) described the structure-guided discovery of PLX4032 (RG7204), a potent inhibitor of oncogenic B-RAF(V600E) kinase activity that selectively blocked the RAF/MEK/ERK pathway in BRAF-mutant cells and caused regression of BRAF-mutant xenografts. It had no effect on melanoma xenografts with wildtype BRAF. In a Phase 1 trial, 24 of 32 patients with BRAF-mutant metastatic melanoma treated at the maximum tolerated dose of 960 mg twice daily had partial responses and 2 had complete responses, an 81% response rate.
quotes: Preclinical experiments demonstrated that PLX4032 selectively blocked the RAF/MEK/ERK pathway in BRAF mutant cells and caused regression of BRAF mutant xenografts.
Out of the 32 patients treated at this dose, 24 experienced tumor regressions qualifying as PRs and two patients had CRs.
Indeed, the Phase 1 clinical data revealed a remarkably high 81% response rate in metastatic melanoma patients treated at an oral dose of 960 mg twice daily.

findings.statement: Bollag et al. (2010) reported that, during dose escalation, 21 patients with metastatic melanoma (16 with and 5 without BRAF mutations) were treated at exposures with AUC greater than 300 microM-h. Ten BRAF-mutant patients had partial responses and 1 had a complete response, whereas none of the patients without BRAF mutations had a partial response. Two responders lacked the V600E mutation and instead carried BRAF V600K; they were among the better responders, with 71% and 100% reductions in tumor dimensions.
quotes: Ten patients with BRAF-mutant melanoma achieved tumor regressions qualifying as partial responses (PR, by Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumors [RECIST 1.0], >30% reduction in tumor dimensions) and one patient had a complete response (CR); none of the patients with melanomas lacking BRAF mutations achieved PR.

Interestingly, subsequent sequencing revealed that tumors from the two patients lacking the BRAFV600E mutation were found to carry the BRAFV600K mutation and were among the better responders (71% and 100% reduction in tumor dimensions)

findings.statement: Bollag et al. (2010) found in paired tumor biopsies that more than 80% inhibition of cytoplasmic ERK phosphorylation correlated with tumor regression. Patients with plasma exposures below 300 microM-h had no measurable tumor reduction. The authors suggested that near-complete inhibition of ERK signaling may be needed for a significant tumor response.
quotes: In patients with tumor regressions, pathway analysis typically showed greater than 80% inhibition of cytoplasmic ERK phosphorylation (Figure 3C). This result indicates that near-complete inhibition of ERK signaling may be needed for significant tumor response.
Patients exposed to plasma levels of PLX4032 less than 300 μM·h experienced no measurable decreases in tumor burden.

findings.statement: Bollag et al. (2010) reported that 31% of patients treated at the maximum tolerated dose developed cutaneous squamous cell carcinomas of the keratoacanthoma type, usually within a few months in sun-exposed skin. These lesions were resected, and no patient discontinued treatment because of them. The authors attributed these lesions in part to paradoxical activation of the RAF/MEK/ERK pathway through RAF dimerization in cells with activated RAS.
quotes: Thirty-one percent of the patients treated at the MTD developed skin lesions described as cutaneous squamous cell carcinomas, keratoacanthoma type.
This paradoxical activation occurs in cells in which RAS is activated either by mutation or by some other priming event.

phenotypes.text: cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma, keratoacanthoma type
phenotypes.hpo_label: Squamous cell carcinoma of the skin

relevance_reason: Phase 1 trial of the BRAF inhibitor PLX4032 in metastatic melanoma carrying the somatic BRAF V600E mutation. It is relevant to the treatment (clinical management) of cutaneous malignant melanoma.

findings.statement: Flaherty et al. (2010) ran a multicenter phase 1 dose-escalation trial of PLX4032 (RG7204), an oral inhibitor of mutated BRAF, given twice daily. Of 55 patients in the dose-escalation phase, 49 had melanoma. Among the 16 patients whose melanomas carried the V600E BRAF mutation and who received 240 mg or more twice daily, 10 had a partial response and 1 had a complete response (69%). Responses occurred at all metastatic sites, including liver, small bowel, and bone, and lasted from 2 to more than 18 months.
quotes: In the dose-escalation cohort, among the 16 patients with melanoma whose tumors carried the V600E BRAF mutation and who were receiving 240 mg or more of PLX4032 twice daily, 10 had a partial response and 1 had a complete response.
Responses were seen at all sites of metastatic disease, including the liver, small bowel, and bone (Fig. 2C). The duration of the response ranged from 2 to more than 18 months

findings.statement: Flaherty et al. (2010) treated an extension cohort of 32 patients with metastatic melanoma carrying the V600E BRAF mutation with PLX4032 at the recommended phase 2 dose of 960 mg twice daily. Of these, 26 (81%) responded: 2 had a complete response and 24 had a partial response. Estimated median progression-free survival was more than 7 months. None of 5 patients with melanomas lacking a BRAF mutation showed tumor regression.
quotes: A total of 26 of the 32 patients had a response (81%), with a complete response in 2 patients and a partial response in 24 patients (Fig. 3A).
A total of 5 patients with metastatic melanoma whose tumors did not have a BRAF mutation received doses of 240 mg or more twice daily. None had evidence of tumor regression during the study

findings.statement: Flaherty et al. (2010) reported that tumor biopsies from 7 extension-cohort patients showed markedly lower phosphorylated ERK, cyclin D1, and Ki-67 at day 15 of PLX4032 treatment than at baseline. The authors suggested that this reflected inhibition of the MAP kinase pathway. Tumor FDG uptake also fell markedly at day 15 in virtually all patients.
quotes: Tumor levels of phosphorylated ERK, cyclin D1, and Ki-67 were markedly reduced at day 15 as compared with baseline in all specimens tested (Fig. 2A). This finding suggests that PLX4032 inhibited the MAP kinase pathway, resulting in decreased cyclin D1 levels and decreased proliferation.

findings.statement: Flaherty et al. (2010) found that dose-limiting toxicities of PLX4032 (grade 3 rash, fatigue, and arthralgia) occurred at 1120 mg twice daily, so 960 mg twice daily became the recommended phase 2 dose. Cutaneous squamous cell carcinomas, nearly all of the keratoacanthoma type, developed in 8 patients in the dose-escalation cohort and 10 patients in the extension cohort (31%). The median time to their appearance was 8 weeks, and none led to discontinuation of treatment.
quotes: Eight patients in the dose-escalation cohort (15%) and 10 patients in the extension cohort (31%) had cutaneous squamous-cell carcinomas, with a total of 35 carcinomas.
The recommended phase 2 dose was 960 mg twice daily, with increases in the dose limited by grade 2 or 3 rash, fatigue, and arthralgia.

phenotypes.text: cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma, keratoacanthoma type
phenotypes.hpo_label: Squamous cell carcinoma of the skin

findings.statement: Flaherty et al. (2010) noted that 40 to 60% of melanomas carry an activating BRAF mutation. Ninety percent of reported BRAF mutations are the V600E substitution, which constitutively activates BRAF and MAP kinase signaling.
quotes: 40 to 60% of melanomas, and 7 to 8% of all cancers, carry an activating mutation in the gene encoding the serine–threonine protein kinase B-RAF (BRAF). Ninety percent of reported BRAF mutations result in a substitution of glutamic acid for valine at amino acid 600 (the V600E mutation).

relevance_reason: Whole-genome somatic mutation catalogue of one metastatic malignant melanoma cell line (COLO-829). It describes the UV mutational signature and somatic driver mutations. This is somatic, not germline susceptibility, so it adds supporting context to the melanoma entry.

findings.statement: Pleasance et al. (2010) sequenced the whole genome of COLO-829, a malignant melanoma cell line. It came from an untreated metastasis in a 43-year-old man with no identified skin primary. They compared it with a lymphoblastoid line (COLO-829BL) from the same patient. They identified 33,345 somatic base substitutions, 66 confirmed small insertions/deletions, and 37 confirmed somatic rearrangements. Of the base substitutions, 292 were in protein-coding sequences, and 187 of these were nonsynonymous.
quotes: COLO-829 is an immortal, publicly available cancer cell line derived, before treatment, from a metastasis of a malignant melanoma in a 43-year-old male. No skin primary was identified.
We identified 33,345 somatic base substitutions.

A total of 292 somatic base substitutions were in protein-coding sequences (Table 1 and Supplementary Table 4). Of these, 187 caused amino acid changes (non-synonymous), including 172 that were missense and 15 nonsense

findings.statement: Pleasance et al. (2010) found BRAF V600E and a 12-kb internal homozygous deletion of PTEN by genome-wide sequencing of the COLO-829 melanoma genome. They predicted that the PTEN deletion causes premature termination. A previously known 2-bp deletion in CDKN2A was not detected in the genome-wide calls but was found in sequence reads when a targeted search was made.
quotes: Of the three previously identified driver mutations in COLO-829, genome-wide sequencing revealed BRAF V600E in addition to the PTEN deletion described above. A 2-bp deletion in CDKN2A was not detected, but was found in sequence reads when a targeted search was made.
A 12-kilobase (kb) internal homozygous deletion of the recessive cancer gene PTEN is predicted to cause premature termination and is presumably implicated in the development of COLO-829.

findings.statement: Pleasance et al. (2010) found that most somatic base substitutions in the COLO-829 melanoma were C-to-T/G-to-A transitions. Of 510 dinucleotide substitutions, 360 were CC-to-TT/GG-to-AA changes. In addition, 92% of C-to-T mutations occurred at the 3-prime base of a pyrimidine dinucleotide. The authors concluded that most of these substitutions were attributable to DNA damage from ultraviolet light.
quotes: Most somatic base substitutions in COLO-829 were C>T/G>A transitions (Fig. 2a). Of the 510 dinucleotide substitutions, 360 were CC>TT/GG>AA changes.
A total of 92% of C>T mutations occurred at the 3′ base of a pyrimidine dinucleotide compared with 53% expected by chance (P<0.0001).
Therefore, the mutation spectrum and sequence context indicate that most C>T/G>A somatic substitutions in COLO-829 are attributable to ultraviolet-light-induced DNA damage.

findings.statement: Pleasance et al. (2010) found fewer C-to-T mutations on the transcribed strands than on the nontranscribed strands of genes (2,773 vs 4,058). Mutation prevalence was also lower over gene footprints, in exons, and in highly expressed genes. They interpreted this as evidence of transcription-coupled nucleotide excision repair and of an additional form of repair preferentially directed at genic regions.
quotes: There were 2,773 C>T changes on the transcribed strands and 4,058 on the non-transcribed strands (P<0.0001) (Fig. 2c)
This suggests the existence of an additional class of NER which is preferentially deployed to both transcribed and non-transcribed strands of genes compared to intergenic DNA.
Genes expressed at a high level in COLO-829 showed a lower prevalence of somatic mutations compared to genes expressed at a low level, on both the transcribed and non-transcribed strands.

findings.statement: In a region of loss of heterozygosity on chromosome 1q in the COLO-829 melanoma, Pleasance et al. (2010) compared early (homozygous) with later (heterozygous) somatic substitutions. C-to-T mutations made up more of the early mutations (82%) than the late mutations (53%). C-to-A/G-to-T changes made up more of the late mutations (19% vs 2%). The authors suggested that ultraviolet exposure ended later in the tumor's evolution, perhaps at metastasis.
quotes: C>T mutations account for a higher proportion of early (82%) compared to late mutations (53%, P<0.0001). By contrast, C>A/G>T changes account for a higher proportion of late (19%) compared to early (2%) mutations.
The results suggest that exposure to ultraviolet light was extinguished after the 1q re-duplication event, perhaps when the melanoma metastasized, resulting in a reduced rate of C>T/G>A mutation.

findings.statement: In the COLO-829 melanoma, Pleasance et al. (2010) identified two heterozygous somatic missense mutations in SPDEF, p.S229L and p.D283H. Sequencing SPDEF in 48 additional untreated metastatic melanomas revealed a further somatic mutation, p.W158*. The authors noted that additional melanomas would need to be analyzed to determine the significance of these mutations.
quotes: two heterozygous missense mutations (het, p.S229L; het, p.D283H) were in SPDEF, which encodes a member of the ETS transcription factor family.
Sequencing SPDEF through 48 additional, untreated metastatic melanomas revealed a further somatic mutation (p.W158*).

findings.statement: In the COLO-829 melanoma, Pleasance et al. (2010) also found a heterozygous missense mutation in MMP28 (p.G297E) and one in UVRAG (p.N561K). An exonic deletion in MAGI2 produced an expressed in-frame chimeric transcript of unclear significance. There were also high-level amplifications on chromosome 3p (including RARB and TOP2B) and on chromosome 15, and a homozygous deletion removing the start codon of CNOT1.
quotes: A missense mutation (het, p.G297E) was identified in the matrix metalloproteinase gene MMP28.
A missense mutation (het, p.N561K) was also identified in UVRAG
the relatively restricted region of high (8- to 12-fold) copy number increase on chromosome 3p which contains four complete genes: RARB, TOP2B, NGLY1 and KS (OXSM).

relevance_reason: This GWAS links common variants at 9p21 (MTAP) and 22q13 (PLA2G6) to nevus count, the strongest known melanoma risk factor. It also shows that these variants are associated with susceptibility to cutaneous melanoma.

findings.statement: Falchi et al. (2009) performed a genome-wide association study of total body nevus count in 1,524 healthy adult female twins from the TwinsUK registry. They replicated the results in 4,107 adolescent subjects of European ancestry from the Brisbane Twin Nevus Study. The strongest association was with rs4636294, located in the 5-prime UTR of the MTAP gene on 9p21 next to CDKN2A (combined P = 3.4 x 10(-15)).
quotes: We conducted a genome-wide association study for nevus count using 297,108 SNPs in 1,524 twins, with validation in an independent cohort of 4,107 individuals.

At the replication stage (Table 1) the strongest association signal was observed for rs4636294 (combined P = 3.4 × 10-15). This marker is located in the 5′ UTR of the methylthioadenosine phosphorylase (MTAP) gene located at 9p21, next to CDKN2A (Figure 2a).

findings.statement: Falchi et al. (2009) found a second replicated locus for nevus count on 22q13.1. The strongest SNP there was rs2284063 (combined P = 3.4 x 10(-8)), which lies in the intron between exons 2 and 3 of PLA2G6. Each of the 9p21 and 22q13 loci explained roughly 0.7 to 3.0% of the variance in nevus count.
quotes: The other replicated region on 22q13 (Figure 2b) showed the highest combined association signal with rs2284063 (combined P = 3.4 × 10-8). This SNP lies in the intron between the second and third exon of PLA2G6
The 9p21 and 22q13 loci accounted for 1.5% (UK) and 3.0% (Australia), and for 1.9% (UK) and 0.7% (Australia) of nevus count variance, respectively.

findings.statement: Falchi et al. (2009) reported that the effects of rs4636294 and rs2284063 on nevus count were additive. TwinsUK subjects homozygous for the risk alleles at both SNPs had more than twice as many nevi (median 30) as subjects homozygous for the protective alleles (median 12.5). Among Australian BTNS subjects, the corresponding medians were 116 and 79.
quotes: subjects in the TwinsUK discovery sample homozygous for both variants (7%) had more than double the number of nevi (median number of nevi = 30) compared to subjects homozygous for the protective alleles (median number of nevi = 12.5).
Homozygous subjects for both variants in the Australian population (11%) also showed greater median number of nevi (116) than homozygous individuals for the protective alleles (79)

findings.statement: Falchi et al. (2009) tested the nevus-associated loci in 2 melanoma case-control samples: the Australian Q-MEGA study (1,734 cases) and the Leeds study from the UK (1,274 incident cases and 123 familial cases without CDKN2A mutations). Both loci were associated with melanoma. The strongest associations were rs10757257 at 9p21 (combined OR 1.23, 95% CI 1.15-1.30; P = 3.4 x 10(-8)) and rs132985 at 22q13 (combined OR 1.23, 95% CI 1.15-1.30; P = 2.6 x 10(-7)). In the Leeds sample, subjects homozygous for the risk alleles at both loci had about double the risk of melanoma (OR 1.94).
quotes: variants in these two loci showed association with melanoma risk in 3,131 melanoma cases from two independent studies, including rs10757257 at 9p21, combined P = 3.4 x 10(-8), OR = 1.23 (95% CI = 1.15-1.30) and rs132985 at 22q13.1, combined P = 2.6 x 10(-7), OR = 1.23 (95% CI = 1.15-1.30).
Subjects homozygous at the two loci have double the risk (OR = 1.94; 95% CI = 1.19 – 3.16).

findings.statement: Falchi et al. (2009) used the Leeds nevus-count subsample (903 cases and 485 controls). When the SNP–melanoma association was adjusted for nevus count, the odds ratio for melanoma moved toward 1.0. The authors interpreted this as consistent with melanoma risk at these loci being mediated through nevus count.
quotes: When the association between melanoma and SNP was adjusted for nevus count, the OR for melanoma risk was reduced toward 1.0 and the P value became less significant, consistent with melanoma risk being mediated via nevus count.

relevance_reason: A genome-wide association study of melanoma susceptibility. It identified and replicated risk loci at 16q24 (MC1R), 11q14-q21 (TYR) and 9p21 (MTAP/CDKN2A), and confirmed loci at 20q11 (ASIP) and 22q. This adds evidence on cutaneous melanoma susceptibility and genetic heterogeneity.

findings.statement: Bishop et al. (2009) performed a genome-wide association study of melanoma in the GenoMEL consortium. It used 317K tagging SNPs in 1,650 selected cases and 4,336 controls of European ancestry. Replication was in 1,149 cases and 964 controls from GenoMEL and in a population-based case-control study from Leeds, UK, with 1,163 cases and 903 controls. Five loci reached P < 5 x 10(-7) in the genome-wide screen. Three were replicated: 16q24 encompassing MC1R, 11q14-q21 encompassing TYR, and 9p21 adjacent to MTAP and flanking CDKN2A.
quotes: We report a genome-wide association study of melanoma conducted by the GenoMEL consortium based on 317K tagging SNPs for 1,650 selected cases and 4,336 controls, with replication in an additional two cohorts

Three of these loci were replicated: 16q24 encompassing MC1R (combined P = 2.54 x 10(-27) for rs258322), 11q14-q21 encompassing TYR (P = 2.41 x 10(-14) for rs1393350) and 9p21 adjacent to MTAP and flanking CDKN2A (P = 4.03 x 10(-7) for rs7023329).
findings.population: European ancestry (Sweden, Australia, Italy, UK, Netherlands, France, Spain)

findings.statement: Bishop et al. (2009) found that the strongest melanoma association was with a 16q24 region that includes MC1R, CDK10 and FANCA. For rs258322, the combined P value was 2.54 x 10(-27) and the per-allele odds ratio was 1.67 (95% CI 1.52-1.83). Stepwise regression showed association with three SNPs (rs258322, rs4785763, rs8059973). rs8059973 appeared to be associated with melanoma risk independently of the other two.
quotes: This region includes several candidate genes, notably MC1R, CDK10 (involved in cell cycle regulation) and FANCA (which regulates genomic stability).

The magnitude of the association with rs258322 (per-allele odds ratio (OR) of 1.67, 95% confidence interval (CI) (1.52, 1.83), Table 1) is notable, since it is comparable to that found by a recent meta-analysis of MC1R variants even though this SNP is distant from MC1R.
one of these (rs8059973) was not reported by the Han et al study and appears to have an association independent of the other two on melanoma risk.

findings.statement: Bishop et al. (2009) found that a chromosome 11 region including TYR was associated with melanoma. The strongest overall evidence was for rs1393350 (P = 2.41 x 10(-14); OR 1.29). The TYR coding variant rs1126809 was also associated (OR 1.27, P = 1.17 x 10(-6)). After accounting for rs1393350, no other SNPs in the region were independently associated.
quotes: The chromosome 11 region (overall strongest evidence for rsl393350, p = 2.41×10−14) includes the TYR gene, which has previously been associated with melanoma; the coding variant (rsll26809) is included in the replication panel and shows a strong association in terms of OR for genotyped SNPs (OR = 1.27, 95% CI (1.16, 1.40), p = 1.17×10−6
Stepwise regression analysis indicates that, after accounting for rsl393350, no other SNPs in the region were independently associated with melanoma

findings.statement: Bishop et al. (2009) replicated a 9p21 melanoma susceptibility locus. The SNP rs7023329, within the MTAP gene, reached an overall P value of 4.03 x 10(-7) (OR 0.85). Stepwise regression showed a second independent association with rs1011970, located 246 kb centromeric within ANRIL, which overlaps CDKN2B. The authors noted that common variants at this locus had not previously been associated with melanoma.
quotes: The third locus replicated is on 9p21, with the overall p-value reaching 4.03×l0−7 for rs7023329 which lies within the MTAP gene
rsl011970, that is 246kb centromeric and is within ANRIL, an antisense non-coding mRNA starting in the promoter of p14/ARF gene and overlapping CDKN2B
Common variants within the 9p21 locus have not previously been associated with melanoma.

findings.statement: Bishop et al. (2009) also confirmed melanoma associations at two other regions. The first was a chromosome 20 region containing the pigmentation gene ASIP (rs1885120; OR 1.58, P = 1.25 x 10(-8)). The second was a chromosome 22 region previously identified in a GWAS of nevus count (rs2284063; overall P = 2.40 x 10(-9)).
quotes: A further pigmentation gene has been reported to be associated with melanoma (ASIP), adjacent to a reported melanoma locus recently identified by a pooling study; this chromosomal region is confirmed by the present data
The second nevus locus reported in this paper is on chromosome 22 and was also associated with risk of melanoma in our study

findings.statement: Bishop et al. (2009) found no significant pairwise interactions between the top SNPs at the 9p21, 11q and 16q24 loci, which was consistent with a multiplicative model. Associations were similar across case categories (family history, multiple primaries and early onset). For some SNPs, the effect was marginally weaker in early-onset melanoma. relevance_reason: Functional study of SOX9 in melanoma progression and therapy. It adds context on melanoma pathogenesis and treatment but reports no germline susceptibility variants.

findings.statement: Passeron et al. (2009) found that SOX9 was expressed in normal human skin but was increasingly downregulated as melanocytes progressed to premalignant, then malignant and metastatic states. Overexpression of SOX9 in human and mouse melanoma cell lines caused cell cycle arrest by increasing p21 transcription. It also restored sensitivity to retinoic acid by downregulating PRAME, a melanoma antigen.
quotes: Although SOX9 was expressed in normal human skin, it was increasingly downregulated as melanocytes progressed to the premalignant and then the malignant and metastatic states.

Overexpression of SOX9 in both human and mouse melanoma cell lines induced cell cycle arrest by increasing p21 transcription and restored sensitivity to RA by downregulating expression of PRAME, a melanoma antigen.

findings.statement: Passeron et al. (2009) showed that overexpressing SOX9 in melanoma cell lines inhibited tumorigenicity both in mice and in a human ex vivo model of melanoma.
quotes: Furthermore, SOX9 overexpression in melanoma cell lines inhibited tumorigenicity both in mice and in a human ex vivo model of melanoma.

findings.statement: Passeron et al. (2009) found that treating melanoma cell lines with PGD2 increased SOX9 expression and restored sensitivity to retinoic acid. Combined treatment with PGD2 and retinoic acid substantially decreased tumor growth in human ex vivo and mouse in vivo melanoma models. The authors suggested this pointed to a possible noncytotoxic approach to treating melanoma.

Thus, combined treatment with PGD2 and RA substantially decreased tumor growth in human ex vivo and mouse in vivo models of melanoma.
suggest the encouraging possibility of a noncytotoxic approach to the treatment of melanoma

relevance_reason: This prospective cohort study looks at Parkinson disease risk in relation to hair color and the MC1R Arg151Cys melanoma-risk variant. It does not study melanoma patients directly. It only gives context for the reported link between melanoma and Parkinson disease.

findings.statement: Gao et al. (2009) examined natural hair color in early adulthood and Parkinson disease (PD) risk in 38,641 men (Health Professionals Follow-up Study) and 93,661 women (Nurses' Health Study) in the US. Red hair is a risk factor for melanoma. PD risk rose as hair color became lighter. After adjusting for age, smoking, ethnicity and other covariates, the pooled relative risks were 1.40 for brown, 1.61 for blond and 1.93 for red hair compared with black hair. The association was strongest for PD onset before age 70 (relative risk 3.83 for red vs black hair).
quotes: PD risk increased with decreasing darkness of hair color. Pooled RRs for PD were 1 (reference), 1.40, 1.61, and 1.93 (95% confidence interval, 1.1-3.4) for black, brown, blond, and red hair, respectively, after adjusting for age, smoking, ethnicity, and other covariates.
The associations between hair color and PD were particularly strong for relative younger onset of PD (<70 yr) (adjusted RR for red vs black hair = 3.83; 95% confidence interval, 1.7-8.7).

findings.statement: In a case-control study nested in the same two cohorts (272 PD cases and 1,185 controls genotyped), Gao et al. (2009) found that homozygosity for the MC1R Arg151Cys loss-of-function variant was strongly associated with red hair (relative risk 57). The authors described this variant as the SNP most consistently associated with melanoma risk. Compared with Arg/Arg, the Cys/Cys genotype was associated with a higher PD risk (adjusted relative risk 3.15; 95% CI 1.06-9.37). The authors suggested that the shared links of both diseases to light hair color and this variant may partly explain why melanoma occurs more often in people with PD, rather than this being an adverse effect of levodopa.
quotes: We used Taqman to genotype the Arg151Cys polymorphism which is the SNP most consistently associated with melanoma risk in previous studies.
The Cys/Cys genotype was associated with a higher PD risk, relative to the Arg/Arg genotype (adjusted RR=3.15; 95% CI: 1.06, 9.37) (Table 3).

Our findings suggest that the higher frequency of melanoma occurring among individuals with PD may be at least in part explained by the associations of both diseases with a lighter hair color and the MC1R Arg151Cys variant allele, rather than being an adverse effect of levodopa treatment as previously suggested.

relevance_reason: A multi-cancer association study that found the 5p15.33 TERT-CLPTM1L variant rs401681[C] was associated with protection against cutaneous melanoma. This is association evidence for melanoma susceptibility; the paper's main focus is other cancers.

findings.statement: Rafnar et al. (2009) tested rs401681 at the TERT-CLPTM1L locus on chromosome 5p15.33. Its C allele was a risk allele for basal cell carcinoma and for lung, bladder, prostate and cervical cancer. In a sample set of 2,443 melanoma cases and 30,839 controls from Iceland, Sweden and Spain, rs401681(C) was significantly associated with protection against cutaneous melanoma (OR = 0.88, P = 8.0 x 10(-4)). The authors noted a published study reporting that long telomeres are associated with increased melanoma risk, whereas short telomeres are associated with increased risk of basal cell carcinoma.
quotes: However, rs401681[C] seems to confer protection against cutaneous melanoma (OR = 0.88, P = 8.0 x 10(-4)).

Interestingly, we observed a significant association between rs401681(C) and protection against cutaneous melanoma (OR=0.88, P=8.0×10−4) in a sample set consisting of 2,443 melanoma cases and 30,839 controls from Iceland, Sweden and Spain.

We note that a recently published study of telomere length in individuals with skin cancers showed that while short telomeres are associated with increased risk of BCC, long telomeres are associated with increased risk of melanoma.

findings.statement: Rafnar et al. (2009) found that rs401681 lies in an intron of the CLPTM1L gene and is in strong linkage disequilibrium with rs2736098, a synonymous SNP (Ala305Ala) in exon 2 of TERT. rs401681(C) was not associated with pigment phenotypes (hair and eye colour, freckling or Fitzpatrick skin type). It was also not associated with TERT or CLPTM1L RNA expression in whole blood or adipose tissue.
quotes: rs2736098 corresponds to A305A in the telomerase reverse transcriptase (TERT) protein and rs401681 is in an intron of the CLPTM1L gene.

We found no association between rs401681(C) and either smoking status or nicotine addiction or any of several pigment phenotypes assessed (hair and eye colour, freckling or Fitzpatrick skin-type score) (Supplementary Note).
Furthermore, no association was observed between rs401681(C) or rs2736098(A) and the RNA expression of TERT or CLPTM1L in whole blood (N=991) or adipose tissue (N=662)
