relevance_reason: Case-control association study that identifies an SLC45A2 variant as a melanoma susceptibility/protective factor in a Spanish population. This is relevant to the heterogeneity and modifier aspects of cutaneous malignant melanoma susceptibility.

findings.statement: In a Spanish case-control study of 131 consecutive melanoma patients and 245 controls frequency-matched for sex and age, Fernandez et al. (2008) genotyped 23 SNPs in 6 pigmentation pathway genes. They found that the variant allele of the c.1122C>G (p.Phe374Leu; rs16891982) SNP in SLC45A2 (MATP) was associated with protection from malignant melanoma (OR, 0.41; 95% CI, 0.24-0.70; P = 0.008 after adjustment for multiple testing).
quotes: This Spanish case-control study included 131 consecutive melanoma patients and 245 control subjects frequency-matched for sex and age.

We found that the variant allele of c.1122C>G, p.Phe374Leu (NCBI dbSNP rs16891982) in SLC45A2 (membrane associated transporter previously known as MATP) was associated with protection from MM (OR, 0.41; 95% CI, 0.24-0.70; P=0.008 after adjustment for multiple testing).

findings.statement: Fernandez et al. (2008) supported the protective association of the SLC45A2 p.Phe374Leu variant allele by showing that it was consistently linked with dark hair, dark skin, dark eye color, solar lentigines, and childhood sunburns. They stated that this was the first time SLC45A2 had been described as a melanoma susceptibility gene in a light-skinned population.
quotes: This association was validated by the consistent link observed with dark hair, dark skin, dark eye color, and the presence of solar lentigins and childhood sunburns.
This is the first time SLC45A2 has been described as a melanoma susceptibility gene in a light-skinned population.

relevance_reason: Association study of pigmentation variants (ASIP haplotype, TYR R402Q, TYRP1) with cutaneous melanoma risk; adds susceptibility evidence rather than establishing CMM1 locus itself.

findings.statement: In European populations comprising 2,121 individuals with cutaneous melanoma, 2,163 with basal cell carcinoma, and over 40,000 controls, Gudbjartsson et al. (2008) found that a haplotype near ASIP, known to affect a similar spectrum of pigmentation traits as MC1R variants, conferred significant risk of cutaneous melanoma (OR = 1.45, P = 1.2 x 10(-9)) and BCC (OR = 1.33, P = 1.2 x 10(-6)). The association was robust to adjustment for the effect of pigmentation.
quotes: European populations comprising 2,121 individuals with CM, 2,163 individuals with BCC and over 40,000 controls

A haplotype near ASIP, known to affect a similar spectrum of pigmentation traits as MC1R variants, conferred significant risk of CM (odds ratio (OR) = 1.45, P = 1.2 x 10(-9)) and BCC (OR = 1.33, P = 1.2 x 10(-6)).
The association of all three variants is robust with respect to adjustment for the effect of pigmentation.

findings.statement: Gudbjartsson et al. (2008) found that the TYR variant encoding the R402Q amino acid substitution, previously shown to affect eye color and tanning response, conferred risk of cutaneous melanoma (OR = 1.21, P = 2.8 x 10(-7)) and basal cell carcinoma (OR = 1.14, P = 6.1 x 10(-4)) in European case-control populations, robust to adjustment for pigmentation.
quotes: The variant in TYR encoding the R402Q amino acid substitution, previously shown to affect eye color and tanning response, conferred risk of CM (OR = 1.21, P = 2.8 x 10(-7)) and BCC (OR = 1.14, P = 6.1 x 10(-4)).

findings.statement: Gudbjartsson et al. (2008) found that an eye color variant in TYRP1 was associated with risk of cutaneous melanoma (OR = 1.15, P = 4.6 x 10(-4)) in European populations, robust to adjustment for pigmentation.
quotes: An eye color variant in TYRP1 was associated with risk of CM (OR = 1.15, P = 4.6 x 10(-4)).

relevance_reason: The paper identifies ABCB5+ melanoma-initiating cells in human melanoma, which bears on tumour biology and pathogenesis. It does not report germline susceptibility variants or families.

findings.statement: Schatton et al. (2008) identified a subpopulation of cells enriched for human malignant-melanoma-initiating cells (MMIC), defined by expression of the chemoresistance mediator ABCB5. ABCB5+ tumour cells found in human melanoma patients had a primitive molecular phenotype and correlated with clinical melanoma progression.
quotes: Here we identify a subpopulation enriched for human malignant-melanoma-initiating cells (MMIC) defined by expression of the chemoresistance mediator ABCB5
ABCB5+ tumour cells detected in human melanoma patients show a primitive molecular phenotype and correlate with clinical melanoma progression.

findings.statement: In serial human-to-mouse xenotransplantation experiments, Schatton et al. (2008) found that ABCB5+ melanoma cells had greater tumorigenic capacity than ABCB5- bulk populations and re-established clinical tumour heterogeneity. In vivo genetic lineage tracking showed that ABCB5+ cells produced both ABCB5+ and ABCB5- progeny, which indicated self-renewal and differentiation. ABCB5- populations gave rise, at lower rates, only to ABCB5- cells.
quotes: In serial human-to-mouse xenotransplantation experiments, ABCB5+ melanoma cells possess greater tumorigenic capacity than ABCB5- bulk populations and re-establish clinical tumour heterogeneity.
ABCB5+ cancer cells generate both ABCB5+ and ABCB5- progeny, whereas ABCB5- tumour populations give rise, at lower rates, exclusively to ABCB5- cells.

findings.statement: In an initial proof-of-principle analysis, Schatton et al. (2008) gave a monoclonal antibody directed at ABCB5 systemically. The antibody could induce antibody-dependent cell-mediated cytotoxicity in ABCB5+ melanoma-initiating cells, and it inhibited tumour growth. The authors suggested that MMIC are also required for the growth of established tumours.
quotes: systemic administration of a monoclonal antibody directed at ABCB5, shown to be capable of inducing antibody-dependent cell-mediated cytotoxicity in ABCB5+ MMIC, exerted tumour-inhibitory effects.

relevance_reason: The title reports evidence for autosomal dominant inheritance and pleiotropy of a single cutaneous malignant melanoma/dysplastic nevus gene, which bears directly on the inheritance of CMM1. Only the title was available.

findings.statement: Bale and Chakravarti (1987) reported evidence for autosomal dominant inheritance of a cutaneous malignant melanoma (CMM)/dysplastic nevus (DN) gene, and for pleiotropy of that gene, meaning that one gene accounts for both CMM and DN.
quotes: Evidence for autosomal dominance and pleiotropy of the cutaneous malignant melanoma (CMM)/Dysplastic nevus (DN) gene.

relevance_reason: Cross-sectional survey of skin cancers and precancerous lesions in Parkinson disease patients. It gives context on the reported PD–melanoma association but reports no melanoma cases or genetic data.

findings.statement: Ferreira et al. (2007) carried out a cross-sectional survey of 150 Parkinson disease patients and 146 age-matched controls, each examined by a dermatologist. Neoplastic or preneoplastic skin lesions were found in 35 PD patients (23.3%) and 20 controls (13.7%) (OR 1.92; 95% CI 1.05-3.51). The difference was no longer significant after adjusting for gender. Among the PD patients, 29 (19%) had actinic keratosis and 4 (3%) had basal cell carcinoma. The authors judged the results nonconclusive but consistent with an increased risk of skin cancer in PD. Citing the melanoma risk linked to actinic keratosis, they recommended screening for it in future epidemiologic studies.
quotes: Thirty-five PD patients (23.3%) presented skin lesions that could be classified as neoplastic or preneoplastic vs. 20 subjects in the control group (13.7%) (OR 95%, CI 1.92 [1.05, 3.51]).
However, this difference lost statistical significance when adjusted for gender
Twenty-nine PD patients (19%) presented actinic keratosis and basal cell carcinoma was diagnosed in 4 patients (3%).

relevance_reason: Epidemiologic study showing increased melanoma incidence in early Parkinson disease patients (DATATOP cohort), unrelated to levodopa; relevant to the PD-melanoma association discussed in melanoma susceptibility entries.

findings.statement: Constantinescu et al. (2007) identified 5 cases of malignant melanoma in the DATATOP clinical trial cohort of patients with early Parkinson disease, compared with 1.5 expected for a standard healthy population, giving a standardized event ratio of 3.3 (95% CI, 1.1-7.8), indicating that the incidence of melanoma was higher than expected. They found no association between levodopa therapy and melanoma incidence.
quotes: We identified all known cases of malignant melanoma (N = 5) in the DATATOP clinical trial cohort and compared that to published expected values (N = 1.5) for a standard healthy population.
The standardized event ratio was 3.3 (95% confidence interval, 1.1-7.8), indicating that incidence of malignant melanoma was higher than expected.
We found no association between levodopa therapy and the incidence of melanoma.

relevance_reason: The paper describes somatic DNA copy number changes in miRNA genes and miRNA-processing genes in tumors, including melanoma. It gives tumor-level context only and has no germline susceptibility data for CMM1.

findings.statement: Zhang et al. (2006) used high-resolution array-based comparative genomic hybridization to analyze 283 known human miRNA genes in 227 ovarian cancer, breast cancer, and melanoma specimens. Copy number alterations, counted as significant when present in more than 15% of tumors, were found at 85.9% of miRNA-containing genomic loci in melanoma, compared with 72.8% in breast cancer and 37.1% in ovarian cancer. Forty-one miRNA genes had copy number changes shared by all 3 cancer types (26 gains and 15 losses), and miRNA copy number changes correlated with miRNA expression.
quotes: 283 known human miRNA genes were analyzed by high-resolution array-based comparative genomic hybridization in 227 human ovarian cancer, breast cancer, and melanoma specimens
A high proportion of genomic loci containing miRNA genes exhibited DNA copy number alterations in ovarian cancer (37.1%), breast cancer (72.8%), and melanoma (85.9%)
Importantly, we show that miRNA copy changes correlate with miRNA expression.

findings.statement: Zhang et al. (2006) found frequent copy number abnormalities of DICER1, Argonaute-2, and other miRNA-associated genes in melanoma and in breast and ovarian cancer. They suggested that copy number changes in miRNAs and their regulatory genes may partly explain the frequent miRNA deregulation seen in tumors.
quotes: we identified high frequency copy number abnormalities of Dicer1, Argonaute2, and other miRNA-associated genes in breast and ovarian cancer as well as melanoma
may account partly for the frequent miRNA gene deregulation reported in several tumor types

relevance_reason: The paper describes somatic copy-number changes and BRAF/N-RAS mutations in 126 melanomas grouped by site and sun exposure. It shows that melanoma follows genetically distinct pathways, which is relevant context for the heterogeneity and molecular genetics of cutaneous melanoma.

findings.statement: Curtin et al. (2005) compared genome-wide DNA copy-number changes and BRAF and N-RAS mutation status in 126 melanomas. The tumors fell into 4 groups with different ultraviolet exposure: 30 from skin with chronic sun-induced damage, 40 from skin without such damage, 36 acral, and 20 mucosal. The 4 groups differed significantly in regional copy-number changes and BRAF mutation frequencies. Copy-number changes alone classified the samples into the 4 groups with 70% accuracy, separated the 2 sun-exposure groups with 84% accuracy, and separated acral from mucosal melanoma with 89% accuracy.
quotes: We compared genome-wide alterations in the number of copies of DNA and mutational status of BRAF and N-RAS in 126 melanomas from four groups in which the degree of exposure to ultraviolet light differs
Samples could be correctly classified into the four groups with 70 percent accuracy on the basis of the changes in the number of copies of genomic DNA.
Acral melanoma could be distinguished from mucosal melanoma with 89 percent accuracy.

findings.statement: Curtin et al. (2005) found somatic BRAF or N-RAS mutations in 81% of melanomas from skin without chronic sun-induced damage. Most melanomas from chronically sun-damaged skin, acral sites, and mucosal sites had mutations in neither gene.
quotes: Eighty-one percent of melanomas on skin without chronic sun-induced damage had mutations in BRAF or N-RAS; the majority of melanomas in the other groups had mutations in neither gene.

findings.statement: Curtin et al. (2005) found that melanomas without BRAF or N-RAS mutations often had increased copy numbers of CDK4 and CCND1, which act downstream in the RAS-BRAF pathway. They concluded that melanoma develops through distinct genetic pathways, and that CDK4 and CCND1 are implicated as independent oncogenes in melanomas lacking BRAF or N-RAS mutations.
quotes: Melanomas with wild-type BRAF or N-RAS frequently had increases in the number of copies of the genes for cyclin-dependent kinase 4 (CDK4) and cyclin D1 (CCND1), downstream components of the RAS-BRAF pathway.
indicate that there are distinct genetic pathways in the development of melanoma and implicate CDK4 and CCND1 as independent oncogenes in melanomas without mutations in BRAF or N-RAS.

relevance_reason: The title says the paper covers the genetic aspects of malignant melanoma, which is directly related to CMM1. Only the title was available, so no patient, family or inheritance details could be extracted or quoted.

Describes visual function (contrast sensitivity) in 2 patients with melanoma-associated retinopathy, a paraneoplastic complication of melanoma. It has no genetic content but adds clinical context about an associated feature.

findings.statement: Alexander et al. (2004) studied contrast sensitivity in 2 patients with melanoma-associated retinopathy (MAR), aged 57 and 61 years, who had normal Snellen visual acuity. Both patients had lower contrast sensitivity than 10 normal observers. With the steady-pedestal paradigm (presumed to reflect the magnocellular pathway), the loss was greatest at the lowest spatial frequency (0.25 cpd). With the pulsed-pedestal paradigm (presumed to reflect the parvocellular pathway), the loss was greatest at 1 cpd. Sensitivity was normal at 8 cpd. The authors concluded that the deficits were not specific to the magnocellular pathway. They said the deficits instead depended on spatial frequency and were consistent with retinal bipolar cell dysfunction.
quotes: Two patients with MAR, ages 57 and 61 years, with normal Snellen visual acuity, participated in the study.
Both patients with MAR showed a loss of contrast sensitivity compared to normal observers, but the pattern of loss differed for the two testing paradigms.

The overall pattern of contrast sensitivity loss shown by the patients with MAR is consistent with the dysfunction at the level of the retinal bipolar cells that is presumed to underlie the MAR syndrome.

findings.statement: MOSCHELLA (1961) reported malignant melanoma of the skin in sisters.
quotes: A report of malignant melanoma of the skin in sisters.

findings.statement: SCHOCH (1963) reported a pedigree study and a cytogenetic study of familial malignant melanoma.
quotes: FAMILIAL MALIGNANT MELANOMA. A PEDIGREE AND CYTOGENETIC STUDY.

findings.statement: SALAMON et al. (1963) reported on the question of whether malignant melanoma is hereditary.
quotes: A contribution to the question of heredity of malignant melanomas.

relevance_reason: Genomewide linkage study of familial cutaneous malignant melanoma without CDKN2A/CDK4 involvement that maps a susceptibility locus to chromosome 1p. This is mapping evidence a curator would cite for chromosome 1 melanoma susceptibility.

findings.statement: Gillanders et al. (2003) ran a genomewide linkage scan in 49 Australian pedigrees, each with at least 3 cases of cutaneous malignant melanoma, in which CDKN2A and CDK4 involvement had been excluded. The highest 2-point parametric lod score was 1.82 (theta = 0.2) at D1S2726 on 1p22. In 9 families selected for early age at onset, the parametric lod score was 4.65 (theta = 0) and the nonparametric lod score was 4.19 at D1S2779. Additional typing in this subset gave 7 adjacent markers with lod scores above 3, with the highest parametric lod score of 4.95 (theta = 0) and a nonparametric lod score of 5.37 at D1S2776.
quotes: we have performed a genomewide scan for linkage in 49 Australian pedigrees containing at least three CMM cases, in which CDKN2A and CDK4 involvement has been excluded
A parametric LOD score of 4.65 (theta=0) and a nonparametric LOD score of 4.19 were found at D1S2779 in nine families selected for early age at onset.
Additional typing yielded seven adjacent markers with LOD scores >3 in this subset, with the highest parametric LOD score, 4.95 (theta=0) (nonparametric LOD score 5.37), at D1S2776.

findings.statement: Gillanders et al. (2003) analyzed 33 additional multiplex melanoma families from several continents and found further evidence for linkage to 1p22, again strongest in families with the earliest mean age at diagnosis. In a nonparametric ordered sequential analysis based on the average age at diagnosis in each family, the highest lod score was 6.43 at D1S2779, reached when the 15 families with the earliest ages at onset were included. The authors concluded that there was significant evidence for a novel melanoma susceptibility gene in chromosome band 1p22.
quotes: Analysis of 33 additional multiplex families with CMM from several continents provided further evidence for linkage to the 1p22 region, again strongest in families with the earliest mean age at diagnosis.
The highest LOD score, 6.43, was obtained at D1S2779 and occurred when the 15 families with the earliest ages at onset were included.
These data provide significant evidence of a novel susceptibility gene for CMM located within chromosome band 1p22.

findings.statement: Gillanders et al. (2003) noted that mutations in CDKN2A and CDK4 account for only 20 to 25% of families with multiple cases of cutaneous malignant melanoma. They pointed to additional susceptibility loci and localized one to 1p22 in families without CDKN2A or CDK4 involvement.
quotes: Although mutations in two genes, CDKN2A and CDK4, have been shown to confer an increased risk of CMM, they account for only 20%-25% of families with multiple cases of CMM.

relevance_reason: The paper describes an online database of germline variants in loci for familial melanoma susceptibility (CDKN2A, CDK4). It reports no new patients or variants, but it is a resource a curator might cite.

findings.statement: Fung et al. (2003) described eMelanoBase, an online locus-specific database set up by the international Melanoma Genetics Consortium. It collects germline variants seen in all loci implicated in familial melanoma susceptibility, mainly CDKN2A and, rarely, CDK4. The core dataset records nucleotide variants at the genomic and transcript levels, amino acid variants, and citations. The ancillary dataset records keyword descriptions of effects on transcription and translation, along with epidemiologic data.
quotes: As an initiative of the international Melanoma Genetics Consortium, we have therefore established a database of germline variants observed in all loci implicated in familial melanoma susceptibility.

The core dataset includes the nucleotide variants on the genomic and transcript levels, amino acid variants, and citation. The ancillary dataset includes keyword description of events at the transcription and translation levels and epidemiological data.

findings.statement: Fung et al. (2003) noted that the CDKN2A locus encodes 2 unrelated proteins from alternatively spliced transcripts read in different frames. The alpha transcript (exons 1-alpha, 2, and 3) produces p16INK4A, and the beta transcript (exons 1-beta and 2) produces p14ARF. They stated that exon 2 mutations can impair both proteins. They also stated that insertions and deletions in exons 1-alpha, 1-beta, and 2 could in theory produce p16INK4A-p14ARF fusion proteins, which existing databases did not take into account.
quotes: The alpha transcript (exons 1alpha, 2, and 3) produces the p16INK4A cyclin-dependent kinase inhibitor, while the beta transcript (exons 1beta and 2) is translated as p14ARF, a stabilizing factor of p53 levels through binding to MDM2.
Mutations in exon 2 can impair both polypeptides and insertions and deletions in exons 1alpha, 1beta, and 2, which can theoretically generate p16INK4A-p14ARF fusion proteins.

relevance_reason: This paper reports somatic BRAF V599E mutations in melanomas and nevi. It gives context on BRAF's role in melanocytic neoplasia. It does not describe germline susceptibility.

findings.statement: Pollock et al. (2003) performed mutation analysis on microdissected melanoma and nevus samples. They found BRAF mutations causing the V599E amino acid substitution in 41 of 60 (68%) melanoma metastases, 4 of 5 (80%) primary melanomas, and, unexpectedly, 63 of 77 (82%) nevi. The authors suggested that mutational activation of the RAS/RAF/MAPK pathway in nevi is a critical step in starting melanocytic neoplasia but is not enough on its own to cause melanoma.
quotes: We observed mutations resulting in the V599E amino-acid substitution in 41 of 60 (68%) melanoma metastases, 4 of 5 (80%) primary melanomas and, unexpectedly, in 63 of 77 (82%) nevi.
These data suggest that mutational activation of the RAS/RAF/MAPK pathway in nevi is a critical step in the initiation of melanocytic neoplasia but alone is insufficient for melanoma tumorigenesis.

relevance_reason: Prospective clinical and histologic natural-history study of dysplastic nevi and melanoma in melanoma-prone families with CDKN2A, CDK4, or unidentified mutations; adds clinical context for familial melanoma susceptibility.

findings.statement: Tucker et al. (2002) followed 33 melanoma-prone families, each with more than 2 living members with invasive melanoma, for up to 25 years. A total of 844 family members were examined and photographed, and melanocytic lesions were photographed in sequence and examined histologically when removed. All of the families had members with dysplastic nevi and melanoma. Most dysplastic nevi stayed stable or regressed, and few changed in a way that should raise concern for melanoma. The authors concluded that with careful surveillance, melanomas can be found early.
quotes: Thirty-three families with > 2 living members with invasive melanoma were evaluated clinically and followed prospectively for up to 25 years.
All the families were found to have members with dysplastic nevi and melanoma
The majority of dysplastic nevi either remain stable or regress; few change in a manner that should cause concern for melanoma. With careful surveillance, melanomas can be found early.

findings.statement: Of the 33 melanoma-prone families studied by Tucker et al. (2002), 17 had germline CDKN2A mutations, 2 had CDK4 mutations, and 14 had no mutation identified in either gene. The melanomas and dysplastic nevi in these families did not appear to differ by the type of mutation identified.
quotes: 17 had mutations in CDKN2A, 2 had mutations in CDK4, and 14 had no mutations in either gene identified.
The melanomas and dysplastic nevi that were found to occur in the study families did not appear to vary by the type of mutation identified in the families.

relevance_reason: Case report of melanoma-associated retinopathy, a paraneoplastic complication of cutaneous melanoma, with autoantibodies to transducin. It fits the melanoma entry as an associated feature. It reports no genetic findings.

findings.statement: Potter et al. (2002) described a 32-year-old woman with a history of metastatic melanoma who developed melanoma-associated retinopathy, with reduced vision in both eyes. Electroretinography showed a 'negative' B-wave, and Goldmann perimetry showed paracentral and central scotomas. Western blotting of her serum showed antibodies to retinal transducin, but immunohistochemistry found no immunoreactivity to retinal bipolar cells. The authors concluded that melanoma-associated retinopathy can be related to a variety of antiretinal antibodies and identified transducin as a novel antigen in this condition.
quotes: A 32-year-old woman with a history of metastatic melanoma presented with bilateral decreased visual acuity.

Electroretinography showed a "negative" B-wave. Paracentral and central scotomas were observed on Goldmann perimetry. Antibodies to a retinal transducin were demonstrated by Western blotting. No immunoreactivity to retinal bipolar cells was detected by immunohistochemistry.

findings.statement: In a systematic screen of signaling pathway genes in human cancer, Davies et al. All mutations were within the kinase domain, and a single substitution, V599E, accounted for 80% of them.

All mutations are within the kinase domain, with a single substitution (V599E) accounting for 80%.

findings.statement: Davies et al. (2002) showed that mutated BRAF proteins had elevated kinase activity and transformed NIH3T3 cells. it may provide new therapeutic opportunities in malignant melanoma.

findings.statement: Noonan et al. (2001) used a genetically engineered mouse model to show that a single dose of burning ultraviolet radiation given to neonates, but not to adults, was necessary and sufficient to induce tumors resembling human melanoma, with high penetrance. The authors concluded that their results provided experimental support for epidemiologic evidence that childhood sunburn poses a significant risk of developing melanoma.
quotes: Here we use a genetically engineered mouse model to show that a single dose of burning ultraviolet radiation to neonates, but not adults, is necessary and sufficient to induce tumours with high penetrance which are reminiscent of human melanoma.
Our results provide experimental support for epidemiological evidence that childhood sunburn poses a significant risk of developing this potentially fatal disease.

findings.statement: Hejny et al. (2001) described 7 patients who developed retinopathy while receiving high-dose interferon alfa-2b as adjuvant treatment for high-risk melanoma. In 5 patients, visual acuity was normal, they had cotton-wool spots and/or retinal hemorrhages, and the retinopathy resolved after treatment was stopped. The other 2 patients developed severe retinopathy with vision loss to counting fingers or hand motions, and their retinopathy did not resolve. The retinopathy was detected after 6 to 26 weeks of maintenance treatment, at total doses of 816 to 1770 million units. The authors concluded that the risk appeared to be greater with higher doses and that patients should be monitored until the retinopathy resolves to screen for sequelae such as retinal neovascularization.
quotes: Five patients had normal visual acuity, but retinopathy with cotton- wool spots and/or retinal hemorrhages with the retinopathy resolved after stopping treatment after detection. Two patients developed severe retinopathy with vision loss to counting fingers and hand motions without resolution of the retinopathy.

The duration of the maintenance treatment before detection of the retinopathy for all patients ranged from 6 to 26 weeks. The total dose received at time of detection of retinopathy ranged from 816 to 1770 million units.
Patients receiving interferon alfa-2b are at risk for developing an associated retinopathy. The risk appears to be greater with higher dosage therapy.

For CMM alone, the highest LOD score was obtained with a single-locus heterogeneity model (Z = 8.48 at theta = 0.0), and evidence for linkage was much stronger for 9p than for 1p, with LOD scores about 2 times greater on 9p. Every case had markers derived from chromosomes 1 and 6, and three cases had abnormalities of chromosome 7. Each marker was unique to its case. Drawing on these results and on earlier reports, the authors suggested that abnormalities of chromosomes 6 and 7 may be characteristic of melanoma. They proposed that chromosome 1 aberrations may be a general feature of human neoplasia.

we suggest that abnormalities involving chromosomes 6 and 7 may be a characteristic feature of MM

relevance_reason: The title shows the paper is about familial malignant melanoma, which is the subject of this entry. Only the title was available, so no patient, family or genetic details can be taken from it.

findings.statement: Wallace et al. (1973) reported on familial malignant melanoma.
quotes: Familial malignant melanoma.

relevance_reason: Reports that small congenital nevomelanocytic nevi, a melanocytic lesion related to melanoma risk, cluster in families. It gives context on inherited nevus phenotypes but does not study melanoma or any gene.

findings.statement: Rhodes et al. (1985) studied 39 probands with small (less than 40 mm) congenital nevomelanocytic nevi (CNN). The probands were registered by photograph in 1982 at a children's hospital dermatology service. Of the probands' 65 sibs, 8 (12.3%) also had one or more small CNN. This rate is 11 times the 1.1% prevalence of CNN in newborn infants reported by a survey of newborns in the same city. In 5 of the 39 families, an affected parent with CNN was also found.
quotes: The 39 probands with small CNN had a total of 65 sibs. Eight of the 65 (12.3%) also had one or more small CNN.
This prevalence rate in sibs is 11 times the population-based prevalence rate of CNN in newborn infants (1.1%)
In five of our 39 study families we also detected an affected parent with CNN.

findings.statement: Rhodes et al. (1985) concluded that small congenital nevomelanocytic nevi may aggregate in families. They suggested that either autosomal dominant inheritance with incomplete penetrance or multifactorial determination could explain this.
quotes: We conclude that small CNN may aggregate in families. Autosomal dominant inheritance with incomplete penetrance or multifactorial determination could account for this observation.

relevance_reason: This linkage study excludes HLA on chromosome 6 as the location of the hereditary cutaneous melanoma/dysplastic nevus susceptibility locus, and it reports heterogeneity among groups of families.

findings.statement: Bale et al. (1985) performed detailed HLA typing in 11 families with hereditary cutaneous malignant melanoma (CMM) and dysplastic nevi. They also re-analyzed previously published data from 19 other families. In the pooled data from all 30 families, with CMM defined as the trait, linkage to HLA was rejected for all recombination fractions (theta) below 40%. When the combined CMM/dysplastic nevus trait was analyzed in 18 families, there was strong evidence against linkage to the major histocompatibility complex.
quotes: Detailed HLA typing was performed in 11 families with hereditary cutaneous malignant melanoma (CMM) and dysplastic nevi to determine if the melanoma susceptibility locus was genetically linked to the major histocompatibility complex.
When data from all 30 families were pooled and CMM was defined as the disease trait, the hypothesis of linkage was rejected for all values of recombination (theta) less than 40%.
Linkage analysis between the combined CMM/DN trait and HLA provided strong evidence against this hypothesis.

findings.statement: Bale et al. (1985) found significant heterogeneity when they compared different subgroups of families in the HLA linkage analysis. They suggested that preferential reporting of positive linkage results and misclassification of subjects' CMM susceptibility status may have contributed to the earlier belief that the hereditary melanoma gene was linked to HLA.
quotes: Significant heterogeneity was observed when various sub-groups of families were compared; these data suggested that preferential reporting of positive linkage findings and misclassification of study subjects' CMM susceptibility status may have contributed to previous beliefs that the hereditary melanoma gene was linked to HLA.

findings.statement: Bale et al. (1985) described dysplastic nevi as a well-characterized precursor of hereditary cutaneous malignant melanoma.
quotes: dysplastic nevi (DN), a well-characterized precursor of hereditary CMM

relevance_reason: The title shows that the paper is about the familial dysplastic nevus syndrome, in which dysplastic nevi are acquired precursors of cutaneous malignant melanoma. That is directly relevant to familial melanoma susceptibility (CMM1). Only the title was available, so few details can be extracted.

findings.statement: Greene et al. (1985) described the familial dysplastic nevus syndrome and characterized dysplastic nevi as acquired precursors of cutaneous malignant melanoma.
quotes: Acquired precursors of cutaneous malignant melanoma. The familial dysplastic nevus syndrome.

relevance_reason: A cytogenetic report of a melanoma brain metastasis that found an i(6p) marker, supporting the involvement of chromosome 6 in melanoma.

findings.statement: Rey et al. (1985) performed G-banding cytogenetic analysis on direct and in vitro preparations of a malignant melanoma that had spread to the brain. The tumor had a pseudodiploid modal chromosome number and 5 marker chromosomes, one of which was an i(6p). The authors stated that this result agreed with earlier reports that chromosome 6 is preferentially involved in malignant melanoma.
quotes: Cytogenetic analysis by G-banding of direct and preparations of a malignant melanoma metastatic to the brain in vitro showed a pseudodiploid modal chromosome number, including five marker chromosomes, one of which was an i(6p).
These results agree with those recently reported about the preferential involvement of chromosome #6 in malignant melanoma.

phenotypes.text: malignant melanoma metastatic to the brain

relevance_reason: Clinical cohort study comparing familial with nonfamilial cutaneous malignant melanoma. It describes clinical features of familial melanoma but includes no genetic data.

findings.statement: Kopf et al. (1986) used consecutive questionnaires completed prospectively on 1,169 patients with cutaneous malignant melanoma. Of these, 69 patients reported a family history of melanoma. Compared with nonfamilial cases, familial melanoma was significantly associated with younger age at first diagnosis, smaller lesion diameter, lower Clark level, less frequent nonmelanoma skin cancer, and lower prevalence of noncutaneous cancer. The authors suggested that greater awareness of melanoma among family members could explain some of these observations.
quotes: These data were obtained from consecutive prospectively completed questionnaires on 1169 cases of cutaneous malignant melanoma. Of these, 69 patients indicated a positive family history for this cancer.

those that significantly correlated with the familial occurrence of malignant melanoma include younger age at first diagnosis, smaller diameter of the lesion, lower Clark level, decreased frequency of nonmelanoma skin cancer, and reduced prevalence of noncutaneous cancer.
Increased awareness of malignant melanoma among family members could account for some of these observations.

relevance_reason: The title shows the paper discusses how cutaneous malignant melanoma and dysplastic nevus syndrome are inherited, which bears directly on CMM1. Only the title was available, so the paper's conclusions can't be extracted.

findings.statement: Pascoe (1987) discussed the inheritance of cutaneous malignant melanoma (CMM) and dysplastic nevus syndrome (DNS).
quotes: The inheritance of cutaneous malignant melanoma (CMM) and dysplastic nevus syndrome (DNS).

relevance_reason: The paper describes malignant melanoma in close relatives of children with sarcomas. It proposes that melanoma can be part of the SBLA (Li-Fraumeni-type) cancer family syndrome. This bears on hereditary melanoma susceptibility, but no gene or locus was identified.

findings.statement: Hartley et al. (1987) described 7 cases of malignant melanoma in close relatives of children with osteosarcoma and chondrosarcoma.
quotes: Seven cases of malignant melanoma in the close relatives of children with osteosarcoma and chondrosarcoma are described.

findings.statement: Hartley et al. (1987) discussed an association between malignant melanoma and certain childhood cancers: adrenal cortical carcinoma, osteosarcoma, chondrosarcoma and retinoblastoma. They proposed that in certain families, melanoma may be another manifestation of the same gene defect that causes susceptibility to the tumors characteristic of the SBLA cancer family syndrome.
quotes: The association between certain childhood malignancies (adrenal cortical carcinoma, osteosarcoma, chondrosarcoma, retinoblastoma) and malignant melanoma is discussed and it is proposed that in certain families malignant melanoma may be another manifestation of the same gene defect which results in susceptibility to tumours characteristic of the SBLA cancer family syndrome.

relevance_reason: Segregation and linkage analysis supporting autosomal dominant inheritance of familial melanoma/dysplastic nevus trait and pleiotropy of a single gene.

findings.statement: Using a life-table and disease-free survival analysis approach, Bale et al. (1986) estimated the lifetime incidence of melanoma in sibs and offspring of individuals affected with dysplastic nevi (DN) to be 46%, consistent with a highly penetrant autosomal dominant mode of inheritance.
quotes: we estimated the lifetime incidence of melanoma in the sibs and offspring of DN-affected individuals to be 46%, consistent with a highly penetrant, autosomal dominant mode of inheritance

findings.statement: Bale et al. (1986) performed linkage analysis between the melanoma locus and a hypothetical DN locus and obtained a maximum lod score of 3.857 at theta = 0.08; all families giving evidence for linkage were in coupling phase and the maximum likelihood estimate of theta was not significantly different from 0 (P = 0.1). The authors concluded that the DN and melanoma traits may represent pleiotropic effects of a single highly penetrant autosomal dominant gene.
quotes: we conducted a linkage analysis between the melanoma locus and a hypothetical DN locus, and obtained a maximum lod score of 3.857 at theta = .08
all families giving evidence for linkage were in the coupling phase and the maximum likelihood estimate of theta was not significantly different from 0 (P = .1)
This provides evidence that the DN and melanoma traits may represent pleiotropic effects of a single, highly penetrant gene behaving in an autosomal dominant manner.

relevance_reason: A theoretical analysis of mutation rates that argues against autosomal dominant inheritance of the dysplastic nevus syndrome linked to familial melanoma. This is relevant to the inheritance discussion in the CMM1 entry.

findings.statement: Traupe et al. (1989) estimated mutation rates to test whether the dysplastic nevus syndrome associated with familial melanoma is inherited as an autosomal dominant trait. The mutation rate estimated directly from sporadic occurrence was exceedingly high (0.9%-2.5%). The rate estimated with Haldane's formula was 0.007% to 0.02%. From these figures the authors calculated that newly arising mutations would outnumber eliminated mutations by 100:1, so that within a few generations 10% of the world population would be affected. They concluded that this apparent lack of genetic equilibrium is not compatible with autosomal dominant inheritance of the dysplastic nevus syndrome.
quotes: When derived directly from the sporadic occurrence of the trait, the mutation rate is exceedingly high (0.9%-2.5%), whereas, as estimated with the aid of Haldane's formula it would be 0.007% to 0.02%.
Accordingly, newly arising mutation would outnumber eliminated mutations by 100:1.
The apparent lack of a genetic equilibrium between newly arising and eliminated mutations is not compatible with autosomal dominant inheritance of the dysplastic nevus "syndrome."

relevance_reason: Somatic LOH study in melanoma metastases from one patient, including chromosome 9 segregations; adds context on tumor progression relevant to melanoma susceptibility loci.

findings.statement: Dracopoli et al. (1987) screened RFLPs at 61 autosomal and 7 X-linked loci in cell lines from 6 independent metastases and autologous B cells from a patient with melanoma. Loss of heterozygosity was found in tumor cells at 8 of 16 informative autosomes and at all 3 informative X-linked loci, generally without karyotypic abnormalities in the affected regions.
quotes: Restriction fragment length polymorphisms at 61 autosomal and 7 X-linked loci were screened for heterozygosity in cell lines derived from 6 independent metastases and autologous B-cells from a patient with melanoma.
Segregations resulting in the loss of heterozygosity were detected in the tumor cells at 8 of 16 autosomes with at least 1 informative locus and at the 3 informative X-linked loci.

findings.statement: Dracopoli et al. (1987) found that all 6 metastases shared inactivation of the same X chromosome and identical segregations at loci on chromosomes 9 and X, supporting monoclonal origin. From the patterns of loss, they built a genealogy of tumor progression and a model in which metastatic cells accumulate selectively neutral and advantageous segregations.
quotes: The monoclonal derivation of the 6 metastases is supported by the inactivation of the same X-chromosome and the presence of identical segregation at loci on chromosomes 9 and X.

Three patterns of loss were identified: unique segregations in cells from a single metastasis; segregation of the same alleles in different subsets of metastases; and identical segregations in all 6 metastases.

relevance_reason: The paper looks at loss of heterozygosity on distal 1p, the region the familial melanoma/dysplastic nevus gene was mapped to. It concludes that the LOH is a late event in tumor progression, not the second hit, which bears on the CMM1 locus hypothesis.

findings.statement: Dracopoli et al. (1989) examined loci on chromosome 1p for loss of constitutional heterozygosity in 35 melanomas and 21 melanoma cell lines. They found loss of heterozygosity at 1p loci in 15 of 35 (43%) melanomas and 11 of 21 (52%) melanoma cell lines.
quotes: We have examined loci on chromosome 1p for loss-of-constitutional heterozygosity in 35 melanomas and 21 melanoma cell lines
Loss-of-heterozygosity at loci on chromosome 1p was identified in 15/35 (43%) melanomas and 11/21 (52%) melanoma cell lines.

findings.statement: Dracopoli et al. (1989) analyzed multiple metastases from the same patient, and melanoma and lymphoblastoid samples from a family with hereditary melanoma. They concluded that loss of heterozygosity at distal 1p is a late event in tumor progression rather than the second mutation expected if melanoma arose by a cellular recessive mechanism. Based on comparisons with neuroblastoma and MEN2, they suggested that frequent 1p LOH is a common late event in the progression of neuroectodermal tumors.
quotes: Analysis of multiple metastases derived from the same patient and of melanoma and lymphoblastoid samples from a family with hereditary melanoma showed that the loss-of-heterozygosity at loci on distal 1p is a late event in tumor progression, rather than the second mutation that would occur if melanoma were due to a cellular recessive mechanism.

Comparisons with neuroblastoma and multiple endocrine neoplasia (MEN2) suggest that the frequent 1p loss-of-heterozygosity in these malignancies is a common late event of neuroectodermal tumor progression.

relevance_reason: Original linkage study mapping hereditary cutaneous malignant melanoma-dysplastic nevus susceptibility to chromosome 1p36.

findings.statement: Bale et al. (1989) studied 99 relatives and 26 spouses in 6 families with a predisposition to melanoma. Analysis of cosegregation of the cutaneous malignant melanoma-dysplastic nevus trait with 26 polymorphic DNA markers on chromosome 1p placed a melanoma susceptibility gene between the anonymous marker D1S47 and the pronatrodilatin gene (PND) in band 1p36, with odds greater than 260,000:1 in favor of linkage.
quotes: An analysis of the cosegregation of the cutaneous malignant melanoma-dysplastic nevus trait with 26 polymorphic DNA markers on the short arm of chromosome 1 demonstrated the presence of a gene for susceptibility to melanoma.
The gene was located between an anonymous DNA marker (D1S47) and the gene locus for pronatrodilatin, a commonly used reference gene (PND), in chromosome band 1p36.
The odds were greater than 260,000:1 in favor of linkage at this location.

findings.statement: In the 6 melanoma-prone families studied by Bale et al. (1989), 34 family members had cutaneous malignant melanoma, 31 of whom also had histologically confirmed dysplastic nevi; another 24 family members had dysplastic nevi alone.
quotes: Thirty-four family members had cutaneous malignant melanoma, and 31 of these 34 also had histologically confirmed dysplastic nevi.
Twenty-four family members had dysplastic nevi alone.

relevance_reason: Clinical series of 9 Dutch families with familial dysplastic nevus syndrome/melanoma, describing melanoma natural history and the effect of screening; no genetic data.

findings.statement: Vasen et al. (1989) studied 9 families with the dysplastic nevus syndrome identified since 1982 in the Leiden area of the Netherlands. In these families, 38 persons had a total of 50 primary melanomas. Nineteen melanomas were diagnosed before a screening programme began, 11 were found at the first examination of the families, and 20 were found during follow-up.
quotes: Since 1982, nine families with the dysplastic nevus syndrome have been identified in the Leiden area (The Netherlands). A total of 50 primary melanomas were diagnosed in 38 persons.

findings.statement: Vasen et al. (1989) found that melanomas detected by screening in families with dysplastic nevus syndrome were at an earlier stage. Melanoma in situ made up 1 of 19 melanomas diagnosed before screening, 2 of 11 found at the first examination, and 7 of 20 found during follow-up. The mean thickness of invasive melanomas in these 3 groups was 1.75, 0.80, and 0.54 mm. Sixteen of 19 pre-screening melanomas (84%) were Clark level III or IV, compared with 15 of 20 follow-up melanomas (75%) that were Clark level I or II. The authors concluded that screening can lead to earlier detection, curative treatment, and better prognosis, and they discussed the need for central registration of affected families.
quotes: One of the 19 melanomas in category I, two of the 11 in category II and seven of the 20 in category III were melanoma in situ. The average thickness of the invasive melanomas in categories I, II and III was 1.75, 0.80 and 0.54 mm respectively.
Sixteen of the 19 melanomas in category I (84%) were Clark III or IV, whereas 15 of the 20 melanomas in category III (75%) were Clark I or II.

From these findings it may be concluded that screening can lead to the detection of melanomas at an earlier stage, which in turn can permit curative treatment and improvement of both prognosis and life expectancy.

relevance_reason: Historical review of Norris's 1820 description of hereditary cutaneous malignant melanoma; relevant to the history section of the entry. Only the title was available.

findings.statement: Hecht (1989) reviewed the 1820 description by Norris of hereditary malignant melanoma of the skin.
quotes: The description by Norris of hereditary malignant melanoma of the skin in 1820.

phenotypes.text: hereditary malignant melanoma of the skin

relevance_reason: Linkage study in Utah melanoma kindreds that excluded the CM/DNS locus from the reported chromosome 1p36 region. This is evidence about mapping and heterogeneity for melanoma susceptibility.

findings.statement: Cannon-Albright et al. (1990) studied 3 Utah kindreds ascertained for multiple cases of melanoma and genotyped family members for PND and D1S47, the 2 markers on distal 1p reported by Bale et al. as most closely linked. They found no evidence for linkage whether they analyzed melanoma alone or a combined melanoma/dysplastic nevus syndrome phenotype. Multipoint linkage analysis excluded the CM/DNS locus from a 55-cM region containing the PND-D1S47 interval.
quotes: was examined in three Utah kindreds ascertained for multiple cases of melanoma. Family members in these kindreds were genotyped for the two markers reported to be most closely linked in the Bale study, PND and D1S47.
Both melanoma alone and a combined melanoma/DNS phenotype were analyzed; no evidence for linkage was found.
By multipoint linkage analysis the CM/DNS locus was excluded from an area of 55 cM containing the PND-D1S47 region.

findings.statement: Cannon-Albright et al. (1990) suggested that diagnostic or genetic heterogeneity could explain why they found no linkage to 1p36 in Utah melanoma kindreds when Bale et al. had reported linkage there.
quotes: Diagnostic or genetic heterogeneity are alternate explanations for the discrepancy between our observations and those of Bale et al.

relevance_reason: Somatic LOH study of chromosome 6q in malignant melanoma tumors; supports tumor suppressor locus on 6q in melanoma, relevant as cytogenetic/somatic context for melanoma susceptibility entry.

findings.statement: Millikin et al. (1991) used RFLP analysis with 5 markers on 6q and 1 on 6p to study 20 paired tumor and normal DNA samples from patients with malignant melanoma, and found loss of heterozygosity on 6q at 21 of 53 informative loci (40%). Five patients had allele losses consistent with loss of the entire 6q arm or of an entire chromosome 6, and 4 others had terminal 6q deletions.
quotes: Five DNA markers that recognize restriction fragment length polymorphisms along 6q and one polymorphic DNA marker for 6p were used to screen 20 autologous pairs of tumor DNA and normal DNA
LOH on chromosome 6q was identified at 21 of 53 informative loci (40%).

Five patients with more than one informative locus had allele losses consistent with the loss of the entire long arm (or of an entire copy) of chromosome 6, while four other patients demonstrated terminal deletions of 6q.

findings.statement: Millikin et al. (1991) found that the region with the highest frequency of 6q allelic loss (60%) in melanoma was defined by the marker loci c-MYB and ESR (6q22-23 and 6q24-27), whereas LOH at loci on chromosomes 1, 11, 16, and 17 was observed in only 5% of cases. They concluded that loss of 6q sequences is a nonrandom and possibly biologically relevant event in human malignant melanoma.
quotes: The chromosomal region bearing the highest frequency of 6q allelic loss (60%) is defined by the marker loci c-MYB and ESR (6q22-23 and 6q24-27).
In contrast to the frequency of 6q loss, LOH was observed at loci on four other chromosomes (1, 11, 16, 17) in only 5% of cases.
the loss of sequences from the long arm of chromosome 6 is a nonrandom and possibly biologically relevant event in human malignant melanoma

relevance_reason: The paper describes 8 Australian families with hereditary melanoma and finds no linkage to 1p36, which is evidence of genetic heterogeneity for CMM1.

findings.statement: Kefford et al. (1991) studied 119 members of 8 newly described Australian families with hereditary melanoma. Thirty had cutaneous malignant melanoma, and only 8 of these also had dysplastic nevi. Another 15 family members had dysplastic nevi without melanoma. The pedigrees fell into 3 groups: hereditary melanoma with no associated dysplastic nevi, hereditary melanoma with occasional affected individuals who had dysplastic nevi, and hereditary melanoma with dysplastic nevi.
quotes: We assessed 119 family members of eight newly described Australian families, 30 of whom had cutaneous malignant melanoma. Only eight of these affected individuals also had dysplastic nevi (DN). An additional 15 family members had DN alone.
Pedigrees fell into three groups: 1) hereditary melanoma alone with no associated DN, 2) hereditary melanoma with occasional DN-affected individuals, and 3) hereditary melanoma with DN.

findings.statement: Kefford et al. (1991) found an autosomal dominant pattern of inheritance in all 8 Australian families with hereditary melanoma.
quotes: All families displayed an autosomal dominant pattern of inheritance.

findings.statement: Kefford et al. (1991) tested whether the melanoma/dysplastic nevus trait cosegregated with 8 polymorphic DNA markers on chromosome 1p, including the distal markers D1S47 and PND. They obtained a strongly negative probability of linkage, which effectively excluded the putative melanoma susceptibility gene in these 8 Australian families from the distal 1p region. No other chromosome 1 marker they tested showed linkage. The authors suggested that hereditary melanoma is heterogeneous both in its genetic basis and in its association with the dysplastic nevus syndrome.
quotes: An analysis of the cosegregation of the cutaneous malignant melanoma/DN trait with eight polymorphic DNA markers on the short arm of chromosome 1, including the distally located DNA markers D1S47 and PND yielded a strongly negative probability of linkage.
The putative gene for susceptibility to melanoma in these families was effectively excluded from this region of the short arm of chromosome 1.
These findings suggest that hereditary melanoma is heterogeneous in relation to the genetic basis and its association with the DNS.

relevance_reason: Linkage study in Australian familial melanoma pedigrees that excludes the 1p (PND/D1S47 and MYCL1) regions as the site of a melanoma susceptibility gene. This is evidence about where CMM1 maps and about genetic heterogeneity.

findings.statement: Nancarrow et al. (1992) carried out linkage studies between chromosome 1p markers and familial melanoma in 7 Australian kindreds, 3 of which were the largest reported worldwide. They excluded a melanoma gene from a 40-cM region spanning the interval between D1S47 and PND and extending about 15 cM on either side of these markers. They also excluded a region of about 20 cM around the MYCL1/D1S57 loci.
quotes: We have carried out linkage studies between markers on 1p and MLM in seven Australian kindreds; three of these are the largest reported worldwide.
We have been able to exclude localization of an MLM gene from a 40-cM region that spans the interval between D1S47 and PND and extends approximately 15 cM on either side of these markers.
In addition, we can exclude a region of about 20 cM around the MYCL1/D1S57 loci.

findings.statement: Nancarrow et al. (1992) noted that there was considerable controversy over whether a cutaneous malignant melanoma/dysplastic nevus gene (CMM) maps to distal 1p, linked to PND and D1S47. They stated that no study had found support for linkage of familial melanoma alone to these markers. Their own linkage data from 7 Australian kindreds excluded this region.
quotes: Considerable controversy exists over the possible assignment of a cutaneous malignant melanoma/dysplastic nevus gene, designated CMM, to the distal short arm of chromosome 1, linked to the PND and D1S47 loci.
To date, no support for linkage of MLM alone to these markers has been found; likewise no study has been able to exclude the entire region between PND and D1S47 from linkage to MLM.

relevance_reason: LOH and homozygous deletion mapping in melanoma tumors/cell lines narrowing the putative 9p21 melanoma tumor-suppressor locus (CMM2-related region on 9p).

findings.statement: Fountain et al. (1992) performed loss-of-heterozygosity studies in melanoma using 8 markers spanning 9pter to proximal 9q (D9S33, IFNB1, the IFNA gene cluster, D9S126, D9S3, D9S19, GGTB2, and ASSP3). Two or more loci were hemizygously reduced in 12 of 14 (86%) informative metastatic melanoma tumor and cell line DNAs, and homozygous deletions of D9S126 were observed in 2 of 20 (10%) melanoma cell lines, defining a small critical region of 2-3 Mb on 9p21 in which a putative melanoma tumor-suppressor gene was likely to reside.
quotes: Two or more of these loci were found to be hemizygously reduced in 12 of 14 (86%) informative metastatic melanoma tumor and cell line DNAs, and homozygous deletions of the marker D9S126 were observed in 2 of 20 (10%) melanoma cell lines.
These findings have resulted in the identification of a small critical region of 2-3 megabases on 9p21 in which a putative melanoma tumor-suppressor gene appears likely to reside.

findings.statement: Fountain et al. (1992) eliminated several 9p candidate genes, including IFNB1, the IFNA gene cluster, GGTB2, and the TYRP locus, as targets of the melanoma tumor-suppressor locus because they lie outside the homozygously deleted regions.
quotes: Several 9p candidate genes, including IFNB1, the IFNA gene cluster, GGTB2, and the tyrosinase-related protein (TYRP) locus, have all been eliminated as potential targets because they are located outside of the homozygously deleted regions.

relevance_reason: Early family report defining the familial atypical multiple mole-melanoma (FAMMM) syndrome, the phenotype underlying CMM1 susceptibility, with autosomal dominant transmission.

findings.statement: Lynch et al. (1978) described a family showing concordance for malignant melanoma and a cutaneous phenotype characterized by multiple large moles of variable size and color (reddish-brown to bright red) with pigmentary leakage, which they termed the familial atypical multiple mole-melanoma syndrome. They suggested that this cutaneous phenotype signifies melanoma risk.
quotes: A family is described showing concordance for malignant melanoma and a cutaneous phenotype characterised by multiple large moles of variable size and colour (reddish-brown to bright red) with pigmentary leakage.
This cutaneous phenotype signifying melanoma risk may now be added to an increasing body of knowledge dealing with cancer-related genodermatoses.

phenotypes.text: multiple large moles of variable size and color

findings.statement: Lynch et al. (1978) found that transmission of the atypical multiple mole cutaneous phenotype in the reported family, and in several other families under investigation, was consistent with a simple autosomal dominant factor.
quotes: Transmission of the cutaneous phenotype in the subject family, and in several others currently under investigation, shows an inheritance pattern consistent with a simple autosomal dominant factor.

relevance_reason: Classic clinical description of familial melanoma with B-K (dysplastic) moles as precursor lesions in melanoma families.

findings.statement: Clark et al. (1978) described distinctive melanocytic moles in 37 patients from 6 melanoma families, designating the clinical and histologic features the 'B-K mole syndrome.' Among examined family members, 15 of 17 patients with melanoma and 22 of 41 nonmelanoma relatives had the unique moles.
quotes: Distinctive melanocytic moles are described in 37 patients from six melanoma families.
Among the family members examined by the authors, 15 of 17 patients with melanoma and 22 of 41 nonmelanoma relatives had the unique moles.

phenotypes.text: atypical melanocytic moles in melanoma patients
atypical melanocytic moles in nonmelanoma relatives

findings.statement: Clark et al. (1978) reported that B-K mole syndrome was characterized clinically by fewer than 10 to more than 100 moles, prominent on the upper trunk and extremities, varying in size (5 to 15 mm), outline, and color. Histologically, B-K moles showed atypical melanocytic hyperplasia, lymphocytic infiltration, delicate fibroplasia, and new blood vessels occurring within a compound nevus or de novo.
quotes: The clinical features of the syndrome include the presence of less than 10 to greater than 100 moles prominent of the upper trunk and extremities, and variability of mole size (5 mm to 15 mm), outline, and color combination.
Histologically, B-K moles show atypical melanocytic hyperplasia, lymphocytic infiltration, delicate fibroplasia, and new blood vessels that occur within a compound nevus or de novo.

phenotypes.text: multiple nevi on upper trunk and extremities

findings.statement: Clark et al. (1978) photographically documented the transformation of 2 B-K moles into malignant melanomas, supporting the origin of familial melanomas from heritable melanocytic lesions.
quotes: The transformation of two B-K moles into malignant melanomas was documented photographically.

phenotypes.text: malignant transformation of nevi to melanoma

relevance_reason: Early description proposing that familial melanoma is related to an inherited syndrome of precursor cutaneous lesions (dysplastic nevi) that marks relatives at high risk.

findings.statement: Greene et al. (1978) suggested that familial occurrences of malignant melanoma may be related to an inherited syndrome of precursor cutaneous lesions with distinct clinical and histologic features. They noted that recognizing this syndrome in relatives of melanoma patients identifies a subset of family members at high risk for melanoma, which makes early diagnosis and treatment easier.
quotes: Familial occurrences of malignant melanoma may be related to an inherited syndrome of precursor cutaneous lesions with distinct clinical and histologic features.
Recognition of the syndrome in the relatives of melanoma patients identifies a subset of family members at high risk for melanoma, facilitating their early diagnosis and treatment.

relevance_reason: This paper describes distinctive precursor pigmented lesions (dysplastic nevi) in melanoma-prone families. It proposes them as an autosomal dominant preneoplastic syndrome, which belongs to the core clinical description of familial cutaneous malignant melanoma.

findings.statement: Reimer et al. (1978) studied 7 consecutive melanoma-prone families. Pigmented lesions with distinctive clinical and histologic characteristics were present in 18 of 20 melanoma patients (90%) and in 24 of 43 first-degree relatives (56%). Recognising these lesions led to the detection of early-stage melanoma in 6 family members.
quotes: In seven consecutive melanoma-prone families, pigmented lesions with distinctive clinical and histologic characteristics occurred in 18 of 20 melanoma patients (90%) and 24 of 43 first-degree relatives (56%).
Recognition of these lesions led to the detection of early-stage melanoma in six family members.

phenotypes.text: distinctive pigmented precursor lesions in melanoma patients
distinctive pigmented lesions in first-degree relatives

findings.statement: Reimer et al. (1978) concluded that the precursor-lesion syndrome in melanoma-prone families appeared to be an autosomal dominant trait. They suggested that it may serve as a cutaneous marker to identify persons at high risk for melanoma.
quotes: This syndrome appears to represent an autosomal dominant trait and may serve as a cutaneous marker to identify persons at high risk for melanoma.
